children: Agencies and Their Qualculative Equipment
能动者及其质算装备

In this chapter, I will explore the following question: How do agents go about producing the judgments and making the calculations that allow them to introduce order into the universe of goods and to effectively participate in the passiva(c)tion process?
在本章中，我将探讨这样一个问题：行动者如何作出判断、进行计算，从而得以在物品的世界中引入秩序，并有效地参与被动化（passiva(c)tion）过程？

Market passiva(c)tion and the transformations in goods it implies is not an end in itself. As the word “good” indicates, pass(act)ivated objects or things, qualified and requalified, must, in the end, have a value in the eyes of agents who must then decide whether or not to pay a price in order to gain their possession. However, for agents to be in a position to appreciate how the goods on offer can contribute to their own activities and to engage in the work of evaluation, they must have the skills that allow them to introduce an order into the universe of the goods that surrounds them.

市场的被动化以及它所意味的物品转化，本身并不是目的。正如“物品”（good）一词所表明的，那些被动化—激活的（pass(act)ivated）对象或事物，经过品质界定与重新界定之后，最终必须在行动者眼中具有价值；而行动者随后必须决定，是否为取得对它们的占有而支付价格。然而，行动者若要能够领会待售物品如何有助于他们自身的活动，并投入评估工作，他们就必须具备某些能力，使他们得以在环绕自己的物品世界中引入秩序。

As we saw in the preceding chapter, goods go through different stages of elaboration. A car begins its existence as a set of plans and ends it as a heap of scrap. Between those two moments, the car takes on a thousand different forms. It also meddles in the career of other goods with linked destinies. The universe of a good whose qualification is in the making is a chaotic web of changing relationships between entities that are themselves in flux. The complexity is on par with a website situated among billions of others in the World Wide Web or a species connected through millions of others to planet Earth. Wherever I go, whether I am wandering through my apartment, surfing the internet, or browsing in a mall, I stumble across beings that have been commoditized. If I were not in a position to make distinctions, if I were not helped to introduce a certain minimal order into all of this by separating images and sounds with my eyes and ears, by touching and stroking the material to appreciate the texture with my hands, by analyzing smells with my nose, and by classifying with my brain, then how could I contemplate attaching myself to any of them? All the possible differences lie in front of me. How can I grasp them, put them into words, make them exist, and share them? If I were not able to accomplish these elementary operations, the process of the passiva(c) tion of goods would come to a grinding halt. There would be nothing left but undifferentiated chaos.

正如我们在上一章所见，物品要经历若干不同的加工阶段。一辆汽车以一套图纸开始其存在，以一堆废铁结束其存在。在这两个时刻之间，汽车呈现出上千种不同的形态。它还卷入其他命运相联的物品的生涯。一个品质界定尚在进行中的物品，其世界是一张混乱之网，网中是那些本身也在流变之中的实体之间不断变化的关系。这种复杂性，堪比万维网中置身于数十亿其他网站之间的一个网站，或一个通过数百万其他物种与地球相连的物种。无论我走到哪里——无论是在公寓里闲逛、在网上冲浪，还是在商场里浏览——我都会撞见已经被商品化的存在者。倘若我没有能力作出区分，倘若我得不到帮助，无法在这一切之中引入某种最低限度的秩序——用眼睛和耳朵分离图像与声音，用手触摸、抚摩材料以体会其质地，用鼻子分析气味，用大脑进行分类——那么，我怎么可能设想自己附着于其中任何一个？一切可能的差异都摊在我面前。我如何把握它们、把它们化为词语、使它们存在并与人分享？倘若我无法完成这些基本操作，物品的被动化过程就会戛然而止。剩下的将只有无从区分的混沌。
Drawing from the solutions suggested by sociology and economics, I will introduce the idea of a
qualculative

agency as the active force of ordering the world of goods. A qualculative agency is a collective entity that has equipment and instruments at its disposal that will assist in the task of ordering by establishing lists, identifying similarities and differences, and producing comparisons and hierarchies between goods. This equipment, which combines both numerical calculations and qualitative appreciations (hence the neologism), is not akin to mere instrumentation, whose only use would be to amplify human capacities without modifying them. The equipment actively participates in the constitution of classifications and the shaping of rankings. It represents an active and productive force that contributes to goods’ transformations over the entire course of passiva(c)tion by qualifying and requalifying them. That is why qualculative agencies can be described as distributed agencies, and not simply as capacities possessed by discrete individuals. Furthermore, as several detailed examples we will cover demonstrate, as a result of the wide variations in the qualculating power that different arrangements can provide, as well as differences in their implementation, there is a great inequality between qualculative agencies. The commercial world is profoundly marked by power relations and domination anchored in invisible infrastructures and expressed in the nature and characteristics of goods as they are framed. By qualculating for and with us, invisible infrastructures decide, in part, our differential relationships to the material world in which we live.
借鉴社会学与经济学提出的解决方案，我将引入“质算能动者”（
qualculative

agency）这一概念，把它视为为物品世界赋予秩序的那种主动力量。质算能动者是一种集体性实体，它握有装备与工具，这些装备与工具通过编制清单、识别相似与差异、在物品之间作出比较与等级排序，来协助完成赋予秩序的任务。这套装备把数值计算与质性品鉴结合在一起（新造词正由此而来），它并非只是用来放大人的能力而不改变这些能力的一套工具。装备则积极地参与分类的构成与排序的塑形。它代表一种主动而富有生产力的力量，在整个被动化过程中通过对物品进行品质界定与重新界定，促成物品的转化。正因如此，质算能动者可以被描述为分布式能动者，而不只是离散个体所拥有的能力。此外，正如我们即将讨论的几个详细案例所示，由于不同的配置所能提供的质算之力差异极大，也由于它们在实施上的差异，质算能动者之间存在极大的不平等。商业世界深深打上了权力关系与支配的烙印，这些关系锚定于不可见的基础设施之中，并表现在物品被框定时的性质与特征上。不可见的基础设施替我们、并与我们一起进行质算，从而部分地决定了我们与自己所栖身的物质世界之间那些有差别的关联。
THERE ARE A MULTITUDE OF AGENTS WITH DIFFERENT EQUIPMENT
存在着众多装备各异的行动者

As we saw, the functioning of interface markets requires a structural divide between objectified goods endowed with their own properties and human agents who, on this objective basis, and because they are capable of judgment and calculation, can appreciate the goods’ qualities. In interface markets, the agents are inherently equipped as human beings, ready to activate, that is to say, identify, the goods — to characterize them, classify them, compare them, and establish a hierarchy. There is no question of where agents come from and how they came to be where they are with the skills and powers of calculation they have. Strictly speaking, just as the model treats the process of passiva(c)-tion as external to commercial activity, it also externalizes how agents become formatted such that they are capable of evaluating and making decisions. The interface market is ostensibly established and developed in a world populated by agents with well-defined identities and competencies.

如我们所见，界面市场的运作要求一种结构性的分界：一边是被客体化、被赋予自身属性的物品，另一边是人的行动者；后者在这一客观基础上，并且因为他们具有判断与计算的能力，得以品鉴物品的品质。在界面市场中，行动者作为人而天然配备齐全，随时准备激活——也就是说，识别——物品：为它们定性、分类、比较，并确立等级。至于行动者从何而来、如何带着他们所具有的技能与计算能力来到他们所在之处，则不在追问之列。严格说来，正如该模型把被动化过程视为外在于商业活动，它也同样把行动者如何被格式化、从而变得能够评估和决策这一过程外在化了。界面市场表面上是在一个由具有明确身份与能力的行动者所构成的世界中建立并发展起来的。

In the most extreme representations, the lack of consideration for the processes that produce agents leads to two simplifications. The first concerns the skills attributed to agents. These skills are essentially cognitive (they involve the capacity to classify and calculate), and in the most basic models, they are entirely embodied within the person. The second simplification is a strict limitation of the list of agents considered to be strategic in the description and functioning of commercial activities. The agents taken into account are sellers and clients whose positions may switch, as in the case of financial markets. The face-off between these two groups is taken to be the crucial event during which the qualities of goods are evaluated and decided.

在最极端的表述中，对生产行动者的那些过程缺乏考虑，导致了两种简化。第一种涉及归于行动者的技能。这些技能本质上是认知性的（涉及分类与计算的能力），而在最基础的模型中，它们完全内嵌于个人之中。第二种简化，是严格限制在描述商业活动及其运作时被视为具有战略意义的行动者名单。被纳入考虑的行动者只有卖方与客户，二者的位置可以互换，正如金融市场中的情形。这两个群体之间的对峙被视为关键事件，物品的品质正是在这一事件中被评估和决定的。

This double simplification very quickly turns out to be untenable as soon as one takes an interest in agents operating in concrete markets. Not only are the types of agents involved in commercial activities numerous and profoundly different from one another — the roles they play are not limited to those of matching supply and demand. Furthermore, some agents are heavily endowed with specialized equipment without which they could not operate in the marketplace. The point for us here is therefore to reach a more realistic description of these complex processes.
一旦人们开始关注在具体市场中运作的行动者，这种双重简化很快就被证明是站不住脚的。参与商业活动的行动者不仅种类繁多、彼此差异极深——他们所扮演的角色并不限于撮合供给与需求。此外，某些行动者还大量配备专门化装备，没有这些装备，他们就无法在市场中运作。因此，我们这里的目标，是对这些复杂过程作出更为现实的描述。

I will begin by drawing upon a set of empirically grounded studies that have enriched an overly caricatured picture of how markets operate. Granted, these studies do not go so far as to challenge the basic hypothesis that there is a radical separation between the universe of platform goods and the universe of evaluating agents. They do, however, convincingly show that agents can only rarely be reduced to their bare somatic resources: they are always equipped with extrasomatic prostheses. Moreover, they also show that the list of agents who take part in the struggle for goods’ qualification is generally long and includes heterogeneous agents with very different profiles. These two findings — that agents are always equipped and that agents are also differentiated — is the foundation of the notion of qualculative agency.

我将首先借助一组以经验为基础的研究，这些研究充实了关于市场如何运作的一幅过于漫画化的图景。诚然，这些研究尚未走到挑战下述基本假设的地步：平台物品的世界与进行评估的行动者的世界之间存在根本的分离。然而，它们令人信服地表明，行动者极少能被化约为其赤裸的身体资源：他们总是配备着身体之外的义肢（extrasomatic prostheses）。此外，它们还表明，参与物品品质界定之争的行动者名单通常很长，并包含形形色色、构成迥异的行动者。这两项发现——行动者总是配备装备，且行动者之间也有分化——正是质算能动者这一概念的基础。
ENRICHING OUR DESCRIPTION OF AGENTS AND THEIR EQUIPMENT
丰富我们对行动者及其装备的描述
Economists and sociologists have already largely abandoned the idea that agents, reduced to their own somatic and cognitive resources, are able to complete evaluation operations in a satisfying way.
Little by little, the
homo economicus
of yesterday’s textbooks, that slightly autistic being preoccupied only with his own preferences or states of mind, is slowly moving off the spectrum.
经济学家与社会学家已经在很大程度上放弃了这样一种观念：被化约为自身身体与认知资源的行动者，能够令人满意地完成评估操作。
昨天教科书中的“经济人”（
homo economicus
）——那个只关心自身偏好或心理状态的、略带自闭倾向的存在者——正一点一点地走出这一自闭谱系。

Economists have been driven by a double realization. On the one hand, in recent studies, the image of an agent who simply observes prices, focuses inward, and pays only marginal attention to the actions of other agents in making decisions has given way to more complex representations. An economic agent’s eyes are not only fixed on prices. They are open to the environment. Being a strategist himself, he tries to anticipate and take into account the strategies other agents are developing; sometimes he chooses straightforward confrontation, and in other cases, he prefers cooperation. He no longer hesitates to get involved in relations with others, the relations that game theory tries to describe. In a certain sense,
homo economicus
is becoming social. When he calculates, he takes other agents’ calculations into account.
经济学家是被双重认识所推动的。一方面，在晚近研究中，那种只观察价格、向内专注、在决策时很少关注其他行动者的行为的行动者形象，已经让位于更为复杂的表述。经济行动者的目光不再只盯住价格。他们向环境敞开。他自己就是一位策略家，会努力预判并考虑其他行动者正在展开的策略；有时他选择正面交锋，另一些时候则更偏好合作。他不再犹豫于卷入与他人的关系，也就是博弈论试图描述的那些关系。在某种意义上，
经济人
正在变得社会化。当他计算时，他会把其他行动者的计算纳入考虑。

The other significant advance of so-called “orthodox” economic theory is to reconsider the role of information. The information that agents need to make decisions must be rendered explicit, be put into circulation, and made accessible. In order to make a decision, to undertake a purchase or put something up for sale, an agent needs to know and evaluate the good’s characteristics. Sometimes he can do so directly, but very often, notably in the case of services, the evaluation can be made only once the transaction is completed.

In order to reduce the uncertainties surrounding transactions, a whole set of devices and procedures aimed at characterizing and guaranteeing the qualities of the good on offer and generally backed by governments has been imagined. Among them, one can cite the most common ones, such as systems of “appellations contrôlées,” the name for specific markers of geographic origin within France,

technical norms, legal classifications, labels, or certifications. That is why socioeconomic theories have given ever more importance to the different tools that make it possible to describe products’ qualities and to ensure that the description is correct. Of course, there is no way of eliminating all possible uncertainties, especially since some of them constitute precisely the most interesting aspect of the good on offer. For instance, when I used to buy a ticket for the Easter bullfight in Nîmes, I had at my disposal all the information on the bulls’ provenance, the past performances of the bullfighters, and the weather forecasts, which assured me that I would, indeed, attend an event called a bullfight. But I did not demand to know ahead of time whether Paquirri would earn two ears and the tail! With all sporting events, part of the pleasure of the show is in the uncertainty.
所谓“正统”经济理论的另一项重大进展，是重新审视信息的作用。行动者做出决策所需的信息必须被显明化、投入流通并使之可获取。为了作出决策、进行购买或把某物挂牌出售，行动者需要了解并评估物品的特征。有时他可以直接做到这一点，但很多时候——尤其是在服务的情形中——评估只有在交易完成之后才能进行。
为了减少围绕交易的不确定性，人们构想出整套装置与程序，用以刻画并担保待售物品的品质，这些装置与程序通常得到政府的支持。其中可以举出最常见的几种，例如“原产地命名控制”（appellations contrôlées）体系——这是法国境内标示特定地理来源的标志之名，

还有技术规范、法律分类、标签或认证。正因如此，社会经济理论越来越重视那些能够描述产品品质并确保描述正确的不同工具。当然，人们无法消除一切可能的不确定性，尤其因为其中某些不确定性恰恰构成待售物品最有趣的方面。例如，当年我去买尼姆（Nîmes）复活节斗牛的票时，我手头掌握着关于公牛来源、斗牛士以往战绩以及天气预报的全部信息，这些信息向我保证：我确实会参加一场叫作斗牛的活动。但我并不要求事先知道帕基里（Paquirri）是否会割得两耳一尾！在一切体育赛事中，表演的部分乐趣正存在于不确定性之中。

The existence of such devices, the fact that they are more and more numerous and sophisticated and that they are used more and more systematically, underlines the limits of economic agents’ competence. Left alone, a consumer would be incapable of doing what these various tools accomplish. It turns out that economic agents are dependent beings with handicaps and cognitive deficiencies.
Although people are perpetually engaged in a complex world of transactions, they are able to carry out only quasi-mechanical classification and ranking operations.
这类装置的存在，以及它们数量越来越多、越来越精巧、被越来越系统地使用这一事实，凸显出经济行动者能力的限度。若独自进行，消费者无法完成这些不同工具所成就的事情。经济行动者其实是有所依赖的存在者，带有残障与认知缺陷。
尽管人们始终置身于一个复杂的交易世界之中，他们所能完成的，只是近乎机械的分类与排序操作。

Thanks to economists, the list of instruments that assist agents is now fairly well known. (Sociologists have also made some contributions, to which I will return.) The list includes everything that enables information to be extracted and produced and everything involved in collecting, analyzing, combining, synthesizing, and circulating information. Besides the aforementioned labels, brands, standards, or appellations contrôlées, other devices include manuals, guides, specialized journals, catalogs, trade fairs, private or public demonstrations — everything that makes it possible to know a little more about the goods and to move ahead in making explicit what their qualities are. To these traditional devices, one should add the different electronic tools (databases, mathematical algorithms) to which agents delegate complex evaluation tasks and whose role is particularly important in markets such as financial markets. It is no longer possible to consider agents as isolated individuals. If one wants to give an account of the evaluation work they do, one has to include the entire range of extrasomatic resources to which they constantly appeal in order to put together a description of goods.

多亏经济学家，协助行动者的工具清单如今已相当为人所知。（社会学家也作出了一些贡献，我后面会再谈到。）这份清单包括一切使信息得以被提取和生产的东西，以及一切参与信息收集、分析、组合、综合与流通的东西。除前述标签、品牌、标准或原产地命名控制之外，其他装置还包括手册、指南、专业期刊、目录、交易会、私下或公开的演示——一切使人能够对物品多知道一点、并在显明物品品质方面向前推进的东西。在这些传统装置之外，还应加上各种电子工具（数据库、数学算法）：行动者把复杂的评估任务委托给它们，而它们在金融市场这类市场中作用尤为重大。已经不可能再把行动者视为孤立的个人。若要说明他们所从事的评估工作，就必须把行动者为拼凑出物品描述而不断诉诸的整套身体之外的资源一并纳入。

Other studies at the intersection between economics and cognitive science have further insisted on the intrinsically limited character of agents’ rationality. Finding exhaustive and accessible information is no longer the problem. The issue is more fundamental and addresses the very nature of the calculations and evaluations of which the agents are capable, whatever the quality of their extrasomatic equipment. The activities of the human spirit, by their very nature, are embedded in procedures, routines, or rules of thumb that have been gradually elaborated over the course of history and that have proven their efficacy and relevance through successive rounds of trial and error. Something we can be pretty sure of — and this is already a lot — is that these routines work. They end up calculating and evaluating on the agents’ behalf, and agents will follow them unthinkingly, dedicating whatever calculating faculties they may have, if any, to enriching these routines, rather than to challenging them.

另一些处于经济学与认知科学交汇处的研究，则进一步强调行动者理性具有内在的有限性。找到详尽而可获取的信息，已不再是问题所在。问题更为根本，涉及行动者所能进行的计算与评估本身的性质，无论其身体之外的装备品质如何。人类心智的活动，就其本性而言，嵌置于程序、惯例或经验法则之中；这些程序、惯例或法则在历史进程中逐步形成，并通过一轮又一轮的试错证明了自身的效力与相关性。有一件事我们相当确定——而这已经很多了——那就是这些惯例行之有效。它们最终代替行动者进行计算和评估，而行动者会不加思索地遵循它们，把自己可能拥有的任何计算能力（如果有的话）用于丰富这些惯例，而不是用于质疑它们。

Let’s consider how projects are evaluated in a cutting-edge company that allocates significant research-and-development capacities to perfecting and qualifying new products. Since the beginning of the twentieth century, companies have striven to elaborate and formulate rules to guide their choices and nourish their decisions, whether by simply consulting experts to identify technical barriers or by exploring market possibilities. These rules, which are the result of informal practices (exchanges with colleagues, collecting sales data), have been progressively expanded, made both more explicit and more formal, leading to procedures and devices that are, today, excessively complex. In a pharmaceutical company, the definition of a research program goes through a series of evaluations, mobilizing a gigantic amount of commercial, medical, and financial data and appealing to battalions of experts and calculation instruments that compare, classify, and grade the molecules. These different devices continue to rely on implicit hypotheses that set their limits. Numerous studies show that the sterility afflicting a good part of the pharmaceutical industry for the moment can be traced precisely to its inability to break out of evaluation frameworks that privilege certain product profiles over other modes of qualification.

让我们考察一家前沿企业如何评估项目，这家企业把相当可观的研究与开发能力用于完善新产品并为其界定品质。自20世纪初以来，企业一直努力制定并表述各种规则，以引导其选择、滋养其决策——或者只是咨询专家以识别技术障碍，或者探索市场可能性。这些规则产生于非正式实践（与同事交流、收集销售数据），逐步扩展，变得既更明确又更正式，最终形成了今天过于复杂的程序与装置。在一家制药公司里，一个研究项目的定义要经过一系列评估，动用海量商业、医疗与财务数据，并诉诸成批的专家和计算工具，由它们对分子进行比较、分类和分级。这些不同的装置仍然依赖于设定其边界的隐含假设。大量研究表明，目前令制药业相当大一部分陷于产出枯竭的，恰恰可以追溯到它无力摆脱某些评估框架——这些框架偏爱某些产品类型，而排斥其他品质界定方式。

One of the objectives of so-called behavioral economics is to analyze the different mechanisms that lead agents, whether individual or collective, not to question the behaviors they adopt and to remain in some way prisoners of their behavior. Behavioral economics stresses the empirical study of observable decision mechanisms and in particular the analysis of cognitive “biases.”

One might say that neoclassical economics describes economic agents as they should be and deduces that from what equipment they must have. In contrast, behavioral economics describes them precisely as they are, with their inextricable mix of reason and emotion, cold calculation and burning passions, somatic and extrasomatic resources. This is why behavioral economics emphasizes the part that can be played by certain technical devices, which are designed to draw the agent back to reason and calculation when they engage in an activity that might deflect him from those virtues. For instance, a light or sound signal might warn a building occupant that he is moving to a different price grid for electricity and incite him to adapt his behavior to take advantage of this position. Thus conceived, material devices are not supposed to modify agents’ cognitive processes: they are simply
nudging
them to make the right choice without changing their modes of reasoning.

They do, however, produce a new conception of the agent, of technology, and of the relation between the two. Technology is not considered as a mere extension of the human body and brain, an extension like a hammer used to drive in a nail that would amplify existing faculties and skills without altering them. Rather, the technology plays a specific, active role that only it can play. It goes to the heart of the action, deflects it, acts on its content, and (perhaps) subjects it to a transformation that is not only quantitative, but also qualitative. A nudge that reorients your behavior has nothing in common with a hammer driving in a nail.
所谓行为经济学的目标之一，是分析各种机制，这些机制使行动者——无论个体还是集体——不去质疑自己所采取的行为，并在某种意义上成为其行为的囚徒。行为经济学强调对可观察的决策机制进行经验研究，尤其是对认知“偏误”的分析。

人们可以说，新古典经济学描述的是经济行动者应该是什么样子，并由此推断他们必须具备什么装备。相反，行为经济学恰恰按照行动者的实际样子来描述他们：理性与情感、冷静的计算与炽热的激情、身体资源与身体之外的资源，难分难解地混杂在一起。正因如此，行为经济学强调某些技术装置所能发挥的作用：这些装置旨在当行动者从事某项可能使他偏离理性与计算之德的活动时，把他拉回理性与计算。例如，灯光或声音信号可以提醒一栋建筑的住户，他正在进入另一档电价，并促使他调整行为以利用这一处境。按此设想，物质装置并不被指望改变行动者的认知过程：它们只是
轻推
（nudge）行动者作出正确选择，而不改变其推理方式。
然而，它们确实产生了一种关于行动者、关于技术以及关于二者关系的新观念。技术不再被视为人体与大脑的单纯延伸——就像用来钉钉子的锤子那样，只是放大既有的能力与技能而不改变它们。相反，技术扮演着一种唯有它能扮演的特定而主动的角色。它深入行动的核心，使行动偏转，作用于行动的内容，并（或许）使行动经受一种不仅是量的、也是质的转化。一个重新引导你行为的
轻推
，与一把钉钉子的锤子毫无共同之处。

Whether or not, thanks to the numerous informational devices that assist them, agents have at hand the relevant information, they can get carried away by their instincts, by their routines, or simply by courses of action in which they are caught up and that catch them. When this happens, a signal can remind them of what they end up forgetting, despite all their aids — namely, that more reasonable behavior is possible and that another course of action might be more in their favor. Despite prostheses, calculating capacities can fall by the wayside or be poorly directed unless awakened and redirected. Nudging is a continuation of advice; it is prescription by other means. You are nudged whenever your Apple Watch signals that you’ve been sitting too long, reminds you of a meeting, or informs you to start cooking for your dinner guests. Nudging invades daily life.

无论行动者是否借助众多协助他们的信息装置在手边掌握了相关信息，他们都可能被自己的本能、惯例，或仅仅被自己卷入其中、又被其攫住的行为进程带走。此时，一个信号可以提醒他们那些尽管有种种辅助却终究遗忘的事情——即，更合理的行为是可能的，另一条行动路线可能更有利于他们。虽有义肢，计算能力仍可能失灵或指向不当，除非被唤醒并重新定向。轻推是劝告的延续；它是用另一种手段进行的处方。每当你的 Apple Watch 提示你坐得太久、提醒你有一个会议，或通知你该开始为晚宴客人做饭时，你就在被轻推。轻推侵入了日常生活。

Sociology takes the opposite point of departure. Unlike most economists, sociologists consider that calculation is rare and awkward or even ineffective and impossible. A first way of relativizing the importance of calculation without denying the agent all capacity to choose is to underline the importance of values or norms that frame and regulate reasoning and behavior. There is no denying that agents confront lists of options or establish rankings to group these options and compare them to make hierarchies and express preferences. Yes, agents really do calculate. However, they are also equally constituted as calculated objects by other agents because the framework that delimits and organizes the operations they carry out partly escapes them. Do they really establish the lists they use? Do they really establish all the groups and rankings? Do they really define their preferences alone? Obviously not! In its most traditional versions, sociology considers individual calculation impossible, or rather, that it is mostly determined by
social

mechanisms that are beyond the agent’s control. Agents are acted on more than they act. This is why so many sociologists prefer the term “agent,” which is passive, to the term “actor,” which is active. Choices are mostly influenced by an agent’s class or networks or by the cultural models and the dispositions that have shaped the agent’s behaviors.

社会学则采取相反的出发点。与大多数经济学家不同，社会学家认为计算是罕见的、笨拙的，甚至无效且不可能。要在不完全否认行动者选择能力的前提下相对化计算的重要性，第一种做法是强调价值或规范的重要性——它们框定并调节推理与行为。无可否认，行动者会面对选项清单，或建立排序，把选项归类、比较，以形成等级并表达偏好。是的，行动者确实在计算。然而，他们也同样被其他行动者构成为被计算的对象，因为界定并组织其所执行操作的那个框架，部分地逃出了他们的掌握。他们真的确立了自己所使用的清单吗？他们真的确立了所有的分组与排序吗？他们真的是独自界定自己的偏好吗？显然不是！在其最传统的版本中，社会学认为个体计算是不可能的，或者说，它主要由行动者无法控制的
社会
机制所决定。行动者更多是被作用，而不是在行动。正因如此，许多社会学家偏爱带有被动色彩的 agent（行动者）一词，而不喜欢带有主动色彩的 actor（行动者）一词。选择主要受行动者的阶级或网络影响，或受塑造了其行为的文化模型与性情倾向影响。

Just as economic theory became progressively interested in the cognitive capacities of agents, going so far as to include the cognitive prostheses agents endow themselves with in the analysis, sociology has likewise striven to put together a more precise representation of the ways calculating skills are distributed between the agents and the world that surrounds them. The solutions of the two disciplines are somewhat different. Whereas economic theory often maintains a normative concern and considers that certain forms of market organization and decision formatting are more efficient or more desirable than others, sociology prefers to concentrate on the analysis of existing mechanisms and devices, thus focusing on the world as it is, and not as it should be.
正如经济理论逐渐对行动者的认知能力产生兴趣，甚至把行动者为自身配备的认知义肢纳入分析，社会学也同样努力更精确地描绘计算技能如何在行动者与其周围世界之间分配。两个学科的解决方案略有不同。经济理论常常保持一种规范性关切，认为某些形式的市场组织与决策格式化比其他形式更有效率或更可取；社会学则更愿意集中分析既存的机制与装置，从而关注世界实际的样子，而非它应当的样子。

A first set of studies from the sociological perspective converges with those of economists. The evaluations led by agents and the decisions that follow owe a great deal to cognitive prostheses that collect and analyze information in the agents’ stead. For example, fine-wine markets and art markets have become canonical objects of study in economic sociology for their ability to magnify the use of prostheses in evaluating goods. In this context, we discover AOCs (appellations d’origine contrôlée), terroirs, fairs, specialized guides and journals, tasting clubs, critic groups, enlightened amateurs, salons, experts and catalogues raisonnés, training sessions, comparative tests, labels, and norms. Producers and consumers, sellers and clients, never find themselves face to face, limited to their own somatic resources, empty-handed, with nothing in their pockets. When it comes time to make a decision, a whole crowd of parties is present to assist, prompting agents on what they should think, say, and write, like Captain Daniel’s ghost to Mrs. Muir.

从社会学视角出发的第一组研究，与经济学家的研究殊途同归。行动者所主导的评估以及随之而来的决策，在很大程度上归功于代替行动者收集和分析信息的认知义肢。例如，精品葡萄酒市场与艺术市场已成为经济社会学的经典研究对象，因为它们能够放大义肢在物品评估中的使用。在这一语境中，我们会遇到 AOC（appellations d’origine contrôlée，原产地命名控制）、风土（terroirs）、博览会、专业指南与期刊、品鉴俱乐部、评论家团体、开明的业余爱好者、沙龙、专家与作品全集目录（catalogues raisonnés）、培训课程、比较测试、标签与规范。生产者与消费者、卖方与客户，从来不会赤手空拳、口袋空空地面对面，被局限于自己的身体资源。到了该作决定的时候，一大群相关方都会到场协助，提示行动者应当想什么、说什么、写什么，就像丹尼尔船长的鬼魂对缪尔夫人那样。

All of the assistance may not be physically present at the moment of a transaction, but the protagonists of commercial exchange have always read and heard, listened to, learned, and incorporated the analyses, advice, and rankings offered by multiple human and nonhuman assistants. Notably, they have in mind recommendations made by friends or family members with whom they share social media and in whom they trust. They are immersed in a social and cultural milieu that forged their categories and their references and in a world of devices that constantly produce and offer evaluations, make calculation tools available, and contribute to shaping their judgment and choices. The universe of prostheses offering help and support to agents patiently described by sociology and anthropology is much richer than the inventories drawn up by economists. Beyond material prostheses such as catalogs, tests, warnings, and so on, there are social prostheses such as social interactions or social media, all of which can be heavily technical. This suggests we should think in terms of sociocognitive prostheses in order to recognize all the equipment and assistance at the agent’s disposal for calculating, judging, and reaching decisions, some of which ends up being incorporated into their very being.

By complicating the description of agents and highlighting the importance of prostheses and incorporation mechanisms, as well as the contribution of social and cultural milieus, the types of studies I am drawing upon here have pushed beyond the stylized simplification of interface markets, with its tendency to limit the list of economic agents to the emblematic figures of the supplier-seller and the consumer-buyer. Take the nature of the firm, long regarded as a black box, a mere individual agent whose interests are expressed and defended by shareholders. Drawing on industrial history and organization studies, economists and sociologists have gradually opened the firm up, documenting the diversity of groups and interests that take part in defining the objectives and activities, as well as the diversity of their logics of action and forms of evaluation. These studies have come to recognize that industrial researchers, sales representatives, production engineers, consumers, financial and regulatory institutions, and government authorities, to name a few, do not necessarily share the same vision. Yet all of them strive to be involved in one way or another in decision making, even if they are not always able to impose their point of view.

所有这些协助在交易发生的那一刻未必都亲身在场，但商业交换的主角们一直在阅读、听见、倾听、学习并内化众多人类与非人类助手所提供的分析、建议与排序。尤其是，他们心中记着朋友或家人的推荐——他们与这些人共享社交媒体，并信任这些人。他们沉浸在一个塑造了其分类与参照的社会文化环境之中，也沉浸在一个由装置构成的世界之中：这些装置不断生产并提供评估、提供计算工具，并参与塑造他们的判断与选择。社会学与人类学耐心描述过的、为行动者提供帮助与支持的义肢世界，比经济学家所编制的清单丰富得多。除了目录、测试、警示等物质义肢之外，还有社会义肢，例如社会互动或社交媒体，而所有这些都可能高度技术化。这提示我们应当以“社会认知义肢”（sociocognitive prostheses）为思考单位，以便承认行动者在计算、判断和作出决定时可支配的全部装备与协助——其中一部分最终被并入他们的存在本身。

通过使行动者的描述复杂化，并凸显义肢与内化机制的重要性以及社会文化环境的贡献，我在此借重的这类研究已经超越了界面市场的程式化简化——后者倾向于把经济行动者的名单缩减为供应者—卖方与消费者—买方这两个标志性形象。以企业的性质为例，它长期被视为一个黑箱，一个单纯由股东表达并捍卫其利益的个体行动者。借助工业史与组织研究，经济学家与社会学家逐渐把企业打开，记录了参与界定其目标与活动的群体与利益的多样性，以及其行动逻辑与评估形式的多样性。这些研究逐渐认识到，产业研究者、销售代表、生产工程师、消费者、金融与监管机构以及政府当局（仅举数例）未必共享同一种视野。然而，他们全都力图以某种方式参与决策，即使并不总能把自己的观点强加于人。

As a way of describing companies and the mechanisms through which to evaluate their activities — and, hence the qualification of the goods they commercialize — studies have very convincingly demonstrated that there are inequalities in the struggle between shareholders and stakeholders to impose certain criteria. It often comes down to a sterile, head-on clash between those whose priority is profit and those who call for responsibility. Sociology has further contributed to this movement, not only by refining analysis of the different stakeholders involved in companies’ lives, but especially, as we saw previously, by showing the infinite variety of the world of intermediaries and the devices that participate in the evaluation of goods.
作为描述公司以及评估其活动的机制——并因此描述其所商业化物品的品质界定——的方式，这些研究非常令人信服地表明，在股东与利益相关者之间为强加某些标准而进行的斗争中，存在着不平等。它往往归结为以利润为优先者与呼吁责任者之间一场无成果的正面冲突。社会学进一步推动了这一进程，不仅细化了对公司生活中不同利益相关者的分析，而且尤其如我们此前所见，展示了中介世界以及参与物品评估的装置的无限多样性。

Given the interest of evolutionary economics in innovation processes, it has provided the broadest opening to approaching and acknowledging the network of agents that intervene in formatting market transactions. All the actors who participate in the process of designing and commercializing new products, from academic research to the distribution circuits, via patent offices, banks and intermediate financiers, insurance and reinsurance companies, administrations and governments, user associations, or religious authorities, are by rights included in the analysis, since each takes part in one way or another, at one point or another, in the process of evaluating, qualifying, and selecting goods; this is the process that leads, in the end, to the singularization of exchanges. In certain sectors, such as health care, the innovation networks that bring all these agents together and coordinate their activities, grow and grow more complex in direct proportion to the intensity of the personalization in the treatments that are offered.

鉴于演化经济学对创新过程的关注，它为接近并承认那些介入市场交易格式化的行动者网络提供了最宽广的入口。所有参与新产品设计与商业化过程的行为主体——从学术研究到分销渠道，经由专利局、银行与中间金融商、保险与再保险公司、行政机构与政府、用户协会或宗教权威——都理应被纳入分析，因为每一个都以某种方式、在某个时点上参与了评估、界定品质和选择物品的过程；正是这一过程最终导致交换的独一化。在某些部门，例如医疗保健，把所有这些行动者汇聚起来并协调其活动的创新网络，随着所提供治疗个体化程度的加深而不断增长、日趋复杂。

The analysis of market agencements can be based only on empirical investigations and observations. It capitalizes on the results accumulated by prior studies. First, it recognizes that the evaluation of process goods never operates on a single site, nor can it be narrowly located in time (that is, it is not confined to one marketing agency or to the ultimate site of the commercial transaction): the qualification of goods and their evaluation is a process that unfolds in space and time. Second, the analysis recognizes that the numerous agents involved in these evaluations have tools and equipment: they mobilize sociocognitive prostheses that differ from one agent to another, but are also likely to be somewhat standardized. Third, it takes into consideration the collective, organized, and conflictual aspect of the evaluation processes that fix the characteristics of the goods that become objects of market transactions.

对市场装配的分析只能建立在经验调查与观察之上。它得益于先前研究积累的成果。第一，它承认对过程物品的评估从不在单一场所进行，也不能被狭窄地定位在某一时点（也就是说，它并不局限于某一家营销机构，也不局限于商业交易的最终场所）：物品的品质界定及其评估是一个在空间与时间中展开的过程。第二，这一分析承认，参与这些评估的众多行动者拥有工具与装备：他们动用彼此不同的社会认知义肢，但这些义肢也可能在一定程度上被标准化。第三，它考虑到那些确定物品特征——这些物品后来成为市场交易的对象——的评估过程所具有的集体性、组织性与冲突性。

Each of these three contributions is essential. Their principal limit is that they do not completely break with the model of interface markets, even if they do provide powerful backing for the introduction of market agencements as an alternative model. Granted, the acknowledgment of these points describes agents’ skills in an infinitely more realistic way. Granted, a throng of new agents appears that no one had thought to take into account, which enlarges the perimeter of activities we consider commercial. What remains unchanged, however, is the idea that there is a radical and insurmountable separation between the world of the agents who classify, establish hierarchies, calculate, judge, and evaluate and the world of the goods that are the passive stakes of these operations. The interaction between the two universes is hard to think of and to analyze, given that the idea of the separation persists.

这三项贡献中的每一项都至关重要。它们的主要局限在于，它们并未完全与界面市场模型决裂，尽管它们确实为引入市场装配作为替代模型提供了强有力的支持。诚然，承认这些要点，是以无限更为现实的方式描述行动者的技能。诚然，一大批此前无人想到要纳入考虑的新行动者出现了，这扩大了我们视为商业活动的范围。然而，始终未变的是这样一种观念：在分类、排序、计算、判断与评估的行动者世界，与作为这些操作之被动赌注的物品世界之间，存在一种根本而不可逾越的分离。既然分离的观念持续存在，这两个世界之间的互动就难以设想，也难以分析。

In contrast, the dynamic of market agencements is entirely structured around the interactions between agents and goods. The qualification and evaluation work conducted by agents transforms the goods and in return calls for further evaluation. Yes, goods do participate, in their own way, in their own classification and in the classification of agents! That has been shown by a considerable body of work on distributed cognition and action whose importance continues to escape economic sociology and economics. Unfortunately, the lessons from science and technology studies (STS) have yet to be widely understood. Sociotechnical prostheses do not simply provide tools for the action; insofar as they participate in it, they shape and structure it from the inside.

相反，市场装配的动态完全围绕行动者与物品之间的互动而组织。行动者所进行的品质界定与评估工作会转化物品，而这反过来又要求进一步的评估。是的，物品确实以其自身的方式参与自身的分类，也参与行动者的分类！大量关于分布式认知与分布式行动的研究已经表明了这一点，而这类研究的重要性至今仍未被经济社会学与经济学所领会。不幸的是，科学技术研究（STS）的教益尚未得到广泛理解。社会技术义肢并不只是为行动提供工具；由于它们参与行动，它们从内部塑造并结构了行动。

One way to reexpress the insights of STS is to introduce the notion of qualculative agency. To begin, I will say a word about the work of evaluation itself. What is it made up of? And how do sociocognitive prostheses contribute to it?
重新表述 STS 洞见的一种方式，是引入质算能动者这一概念。首先，我要谈一谈评估工作本身。它由什么构成？社会认知义肢又如何对之作出贡献？
FROM CALCULATION TO QUALCULATION
从计算到质算
To show you the significance of qualculation, I must first review some basic ideas about calculation operations and their significance.
Conflating calculation with math will be the source of many misinterpretations of my model.
为了向你说明质算的意义，我必须先回顾关于计算操作及其意义的一些基本观念。
把计算与数学混为一谈，将会成为对我的模型产生诸多误解的根源。

Calculating does not necessarily mean carrying out mathematical or even numerical operations. This observation is in line with common sense. I can point to numerous examples in which agents seek to obtain results through calculations that do not involve numbers. One speaks, for instance, of strategic calculation to explain a political or economic decision. In French, you might hear an adolescent use this expression to declare they have no interest in one of their mates: “Je ne le calcule pas,” I do not take him into my calculations. This means there is no interest in the other person — they don’t count. The expression “to calculate” in relation to a person means to judge someone to be a worthy friend. To refrain from “calculating” is to act as though they did not exist.

计算并不必然意味着执行数学运算，甚至不必然意味着执行数值运算。这一观察符合常识。我可以举出无数例子，其中行动者力图通过不涉及数字的计算来获得结果。例如，人们会用“战略计算”来解释一项政治或经济决策。在法语中，你可能会听到一个青少年用这个说法来宣称自己对某个同伴毫无兴趣：“Je ne le calcule pas”，意思是“我不把他算进来”。这意味着对另一个人没有兴趣——他“不算数”。用于一个人时，“计算”这个说法意味着判定某人值得结交为友。不去“计算”某人，就是表现得仿佛此人并不存在。

In its most generally accepted meaning, calculation designates the fundamental operation through which one evaluates and orders the world before embarking on an action. It begins when distinctions between things or states of the world are established; it continues through imagining courses of action associated with those things or states; and it reaches its (possible) end when the predictable consequences of these different courses of action are appraised.
在其最广为接受的含义上，计算指的是人们在着手行动之前借以评估世界并为之建立秩序的那项基本操作。它始于事物之间或世界各种状态之间的区分得以确立之时；它经由想象与这些事物或状态相关的各种行动方案而延续；当这些不同行动方案的可预测后果得到评估时，它便达到其（可能的）终点。

My definition of calculation is deliberately wide, but not unique. I seek to avoid the oppositional distinction between judgment and calculation in conventional, but narrower definitions. To calculate is to identify entities, gather them in lists, group them in classes, then set up a hierarchy among these entities in each class, and then, possibly, but not necessarily, to introduce from this ordinal classification called ranking cardinal numbers (grades or scores) and, with them, possible quantitative relationships. For example, one might assert that such-and-such an entity is twice or half as interesting, efficient, or competitive as some other entity. The diversity of the forms of operations associated with each of these steps explains why calculation can fulfill the requirements for mathematical or algorithmic formulations, or it can be close to intuition, to a judgment based on authority, to a decision in an uncertain situation, or finally, it can be tantamount to giving up on deciding. With this definition and the sequence of different operations implied, the oppositional divide between qualitative judgment and numerical quantitative calculation disappears.

In order to underline the importance of this continuum between judgment and calculation, I have adopted a neologism suggested by sociologist Franck Cochoy: “qualculation” combines qualitative and quantitative dimensions in variable proportions.

我对计算的定义刻意宽泛，但并非独一无二。在那些惯常却更为狭窄的定义中，人们把判断与计算对立起来，我则力图避免这种对立区分。计算就是识别实体，把它们汇集到清单中，归入类别，然后在每一类别内部为这些实体设定等级秩序，随后可能——但并非必然——从这种被称为排序的序数分类中引入基数（分数或评分），并随之引入可能的数量关系。例如，人们可以断言，某某实体的有趣程度、效率或竞争力是另一实体的两倍或一半。与上述每一步相关联的操作形式多种多样，这解释了为什么计算既可以满足数学表述或算法表述的要求，也可以接近直觉，接近基于权威的判断，接近不确定情境中的决策，或者最终等同于放弃决策。有了这一定义及其所隐含的一系列不同操作，定性判断与数值定量计算之间的对立鸿沟便消失了。
为了强调判断与计算之间这一连续统的重要性，我采用了社会学家弗兰克·科舒瓦（Franck Cochoy）建议的一个新词“质算”（qualculation，由 qualitative〔定性〕与 calculation〔计算〕缩合而成）；它把定性与定量维度按可变比例结合起来。

Qualculation has the huge advantage of dissipating the mysterious halo around the irruption of numbers in economic activities and in particular in commercial activities. There is no discontinuous leap from the universe of sensation to that of words and values and then to that of numbers. The movement leading to classification, ranking, ordinal numbers, then cardinal numbers is continuous. In fact, what close observation reveals is that the transition from one to the other is not made in one go. At each step, numbers and words are combined, all the more easily because figures and numbers are also words that, used as such, can have a plurality of meanings that are not abandoned when they are used as figures in ranking or comparing operations.

质算的一大优势，是驱散笼罩在数字闯入经济活动、尤其是商业活动这一现象周围的神秘光环。从感觉的宇宙到词语与价值的宇宙，再到数字的宇宙，并不存在非连续的跳跃。导向分类、排序、序数、继而基数的运动是连续的。事实上，近距离观察所揭示的是，从一个阶段到另一个阶段的过渡并非一蹴而就。在每一步上，数字与词语都结合在一起；这种结合之所以更加容易，是因为数字符号与数字本身也是词语，如此使用时可以具有多重含义，而当它们作为数字符号用于排序或比较操作时，这些含义并不会被弃置。

To confront the enigma of passing from qualitative to quantitative, anthropology has developed frames of analysis quite similar to the ones I am using. For instance, in her work on commercial relations in West Africa, Jane Guyer suggests distinguishing among three steps in the process of evaluating goods.
The first establishes a nominal scale, the second an ordinal scale, and the third a numerical scale.
为应对从定性过渡到定量这一谜题，人类学发展出了与我所使用的分析框架颇为相似的分析框架。例如，简·盖耶（Jane Guyer）在她关于西非商业关系的研究中，建议把物品评估过程区分为三个步骤。
第一步确立名义尺度，第二步确立序数尺度，第三步确立数值尺度。

Guyer explains that an unnamed good cannot exist. The word or the set of words designating a good serve to differentiate it from other goods and to position it with respect to them. Naming is a form of distinction whose meanings are enriched by the usage of words and the semantic networks that connect them, more or less directly, to other words. Guyer refers to a nominal scale the way one speaks of a scale of colors, because the denomination of goods constitutes a primary form of evaluation, one that might be qualified as relational. Indeed, this is what economists draw attention to when they evoke the idea that goods are more or less substitutable, closer to or further from one another, and have values and therefore prices that are interdependent. According to economists, the notion of cross elasticity provides a precise measure of this interdependence.

Furthermore, nominal scales, like numerical and ordinal scales, have the advantage of being both objects that are made available to the agent and objects agents use and manipulate. This observation holds in any Western supermarket. If I hesitate between a package of pasta and a package of rice, whatever the similarities and differences I postulate between the two, I cannot completely abstract myself from a set of conventions, significations, relations, and discourses carried by language and the use of words. Furthermore, I am not the only one to raise the question of whether they can be substituted for one another or whether they differ: this is attested to by the decision the supermarket manager makes to put the two packages next to each other on the shelf. From the point of view of an anthropologist interested as much in the process of evaluation as in its result, it is crucial to recognize this double dimension of denomination. It is both individual and collective.

盖耶解释说，一件未被命名的物品不可能存在。用来指称一件物品的词或词组，发挥着把它与其他物品区分开来、并确定其相对于其他物品之位置的作用。命名是一种区分形式，其含义因词语的用法以及把这些词语或多或少直接地与其他词语联系起来的语义网络而得到丰富。盖耶谈论名义尺度，一如人们谈论色彩尺度，因为对物品的命名构成一种初级评估形式，这种评估或许可以被界定为关系性的。事实上，这正是经济学家在提出以下看法时所强调的：物品或多或少可以相互替代，彼此或近或远，并且具有相互依存的价值，因而具有相互依存的价格。按照经济学家的说法，交叉弹性这一概念为这种相互依存提供了精确的度量。

此外，名义尺度与数值尺度、序数尺度一样，具有这样一个优点：它们既是提供给行动者的对象，也是行动者使用和操纵的对象。这一观察适用于任何一家西方超市。如果我在一包意大利面和一包大米之间犹豫，那么无论我假定二者之间有何相似与差异，我都无法完全抽离于由语言和词语用法所承载的一整套惯例、意涵、关系和话语。此外，提出它们能否相互替代、抑或彼此不同这一问题的，并不只有我一人：超市经理决定把这两包东西并排放在货架上，便证明了这一点。从一位既关心评估结果、也同样关心评估过程的人类学家的观点看，承认命名这一双重维度至关重要。命名既是个体的，也是集体的。

The work of evaluating cannot escape from the (gentle) tyranny of words and the relations they suggest. It is also dependent on operations that institute hierarchies that involve the implementation of what Guyer calls “ordinal scales,” whose function is to institute a series of gradations between goods. These scales allow for the use of comparatives and superlatives. Guyer provides numerous examples throughout her book, showing how the value of goods can be categorized in relation to qualities such as religiosity, robustness, beauty, originality, or efficiency. What she observes in African societies can easily be transposed to Western societies, where ordinal scales abound and are permanently renewed, as the rise of indicators of all sorts attests.

评估工作无法逃脱词语及其所暗示的关系的（温和）专制。它还依赖于那些建立等级秩序的操作，而这些操作涉及实施盖耶所说的“序数尺度”，其功能是在物品之间确立一系列级差。这些尺度允许使用比较级和最高级。盖耶在全书中提供了大量例子，表明物品的价值可以依据宗教性、坚固性、美感、原创性或效率等品质来分类。她在非洲社会中观察到的情况可以轻易移用到西方社会；在西方社会，序数尺度比比皆是，并且不断更新，各类指标的兴起即为明证。

Ordinal scales are precursors of cardinal numbers that bring us closer to the universe of figures and numeration systems, in sum, to what Guyer calls “numerical scales.” These scales give a quantitative dimension to evaluation; they prepare the commercial transaction and the commensurability it implies. As Guyer confirms, there is no reason to oppose judgment and calculation, since one moves to the other in a gradual and inclusive way. And of course, it is meaningless to circumscribe any opposition between rational or so-called prerational mentalities. From the Ivy League schools and les Grandes Écoles, from Auvergne to West Africa, we all qualculate.

序数尺度是基数的前身，而基数把我们带近数字符号与计数体系的宇宙，总之，带近盖耶所说的“数值尺度”。这些尺度赋予评估一个定量维度；它们为商业交易以及交易所隐含的通约性（commensurability）做好准备。正如盖耶所确认的，没有理由把判断与计算对立起来，因为人们是以渐进且包容的方式从一方过渡到另一方的。当然，在理性心态与所谓前理性心态之间划定任何对立，也是毫无意义的。从常春藤盟校与法国大学校（les Grandes Écoles），从奥弗涅到西非，我们人人都在质算。

A “cognitive” vision of calculation, limited to operations involving identification, classification, ranking, and measure conveniently blurs the overly clear distinction between pure judgment and pure calculation. However, the material dimension of the calculation, and hence the link between evaluation activities and the processes whereby goods are transformed through singularization — that is, the very activities that are at the heart of commercial activities, would escape analysis. Linguist Émile Benveniste examined the vocabulary of counting in Latin sources, confirming that there is indeed an intimate link between calculating and judging or estimating.

Moreover, he also underlined a remarkable characteristic of this vocabulary: there is explicit reference to a material movement of detachment (cutting) and of reattachment (leading to a result). This accent on material displacement in calculation, which also appears in the notion of centers of calculation developed by Bruno Latour, helps us sketch a very general definition that feeds into the definition of
qualcul
一种“认知的”计算观局限于识别、分类、排序和度量等操作，它恰好模糊了纯粹判断与纯粹计算之间那条过于清晰的界线。然而，计算的物质维度，以及由此而来的评估活动与物品经由独一化而得到转化的过程之间的联系——也就是那些处于商业活动核心的活动——却会逃出分析。语言学家埃米尔·本维尼斯特（Émile Benveniste）考察了拉丁文文献中的计数词汇，确认计算与判断或估量之间确实存在密切的联系。
此外，他还强调了这套词汇的一个显著特征：其中明确提及一种脱离（切割）与重新附着（导向一个结果）的物质运动。这种对计算中物质位移的强调，也出现在布鲁诺·拉图尔（Bruno Latour）提出的“计算中心”概念之中，它帮助我们勾勒出一个极为一般的定义，而这一界定又汇入对“质算”（
qualcul
）的定义。
Calculation is a three-step process that leads to the constitution of a space of calculation:
计算是一个三步过程，导向一个计算空间的构成：

a) First, in order to be calculated, the entities under consideration must be identified and detached: a finite number of entities are displaced and disposed in a unique space. We have to imagine this space of calculation in a very broad sense: it is the “count” itself, but also by extension the surface onto which the entities to be calculated are displaced (literally or by proxy) and then compared and manipulated according to a common operational principle. It is important to remember how varied these spaces of calculation can be. A bill, a chessboard, a factory, a negotiating screen, a trading floor, a software spreadsheet, a compensating clearinghouse, a computer disk, a supermarket shopping cart (
caddie
, in French) and the “caddytainer,” a device on wheels with deep buckets for moving goods from storage to display shelves that we’ll come back to in Chapter 6:
all of these spaces can be analyzed as spaces, but each one provides a different form of calculation.

a）首先，为了能够被计算，所考虑的实体必须得到识别和脱离：有限数量的实体被移置并安置在同一空间中。我们必须从非常宽泛的意义上想象这个计算空间：它就是“计数”本身，但推而广之，它也是这样一个表面——有待计算的实体被（实际地或通过代理）移置其上，随后按照一种共同的操作原则加以比较和操纵。重要的是要记住，这些计算空间可能多么多样。一张账单、一个棋盘、一座工厂、一块谈判屏幕、一个交易大厅、一张软件电子表格、一家清算所、一张计算机磁盘、一辆超市购物车（法语称
caddie
），以及“caddytainer”——一种带轮的装置，装有深斗，用于把货物从储藏区运到陈列货架，我们将在第六章回头讨论它：
所有这些空间都可以作为空间来分析，但每一个空间都提供一种不同的计算形式。

b) Once isolated, the entities under consideration (that is, “taken into account”) have to be connected through associations made between them. That is to say, they are subject to manipulations and transformations, always in a very material sense. (Think of movements left or right, up or down, superpositions or juxtapositions.) These procedures can easily be recognized when a rule is applied in a mathematical sense or a mechanical calculator is used: as Charles Babbage described on his famous visit to a clearinghouse in the City in London, a calculation-based economy is precisely an economy of displacements. However, these displacements are also at work in less mechanical situations. A financial arbitrageur materially associates two entities by displaying their results in the same window on his screen (for instance, an index and the corresponding derivative, or a company and its target in the case of a possible takeover). Insurers do this, too, when they construct actuarial tables and the associated charts, as do user groups when they make lists of products to compare their qualities.

b）一旦被孤立出来，所考虑的实体（也就是被“纳入考虑”的实体）就必须通过它们之间建立的关联而被连接起来。也就是说，它们要经受操纵和转化，而且始终是在非常物质的意义上。（想一想向左或向右、向上或向下移动，以及叠置或并置。）当人们按数学意义应用一条规则，或使用一台机械计算器时，这些程序很容易被辨认出来：正如查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）在其著名的伦敦金融城清算所之行中所描述的那样，一种以计算为基础的经济恰恰是一种位移的经济。然而，这些位移在较少机械性的情境中同样发挥作用。一位金融套利者在物质层面把两个实体关联起来：他把二者的结果显示在屏幕上的同一个窗口中（例如，一个指数与相应的衍生品；或者在可能发生的收购中，一家公司与其目标公司）。保险公司在构建精算表及相关图表时也是如此；用户群体在列出产品清单以比较其品质时同样如此。

c) A third movement is needed to get to the end of a calculation: extracting a result. The calculation has to bring out a new entity that makes it possible to establish a certain order among different configurations. In its simplest form, this result can be an alternative, or an ordered list that enables the ranking of choices, or a score or a sum that can be compared with other scores or sums. This entity is, in turn, the result of manipulations in the calculation space. To invoke the Latin
summa
, it
summarizes

the units taken into account. This entity is not new in the sense of coming out of nowhere: it is prefigured by the arrangements described above. However, it must be susceptible to being displaced, to leaving the calculation space and circulating in places such as guides, magazines, software, and so on, without transporting the calculation apparatus with it.
c）还需要第三个运动，才能完成一次计算：得出一个结果。计算必须产生一个新的实体，使人们能够在不同配置之间确立某种秩序。在其最简单的形式中，这个结果可以是一个备选方案，或一份能够对各项选择进行排序的有序清单，或一个可与其他评分或总和相比较的评分或总和。这个实体本身又是计算空间中各种操纵的结果。借用拉丁语
summa
（总和）一词来说，它把纳入考虑的各单元
总括
起来。这个实体并不是凭空出现意义上的新事物：它已由上述各种安排所预示。然而，它必须能够被移置，能够离开计算空间，在指南、杂志、软件等场所流通，而不必把计算装置一并带走。
Without these material operations and the devices they require, no judgment, no calculation would be possible.

The configurations of qualculation are diverse. The order book for an electronic stock exchange is a qualculation space (literally in computer memory) where buy and sell orders get ordered according to a set of priority rules. Traders can observe the order book on their screens, explore its depths, and intervene in several ways. The execution price is qualculated by an algorithm. A supermarket can also be considered as a qualculation device. The products it presents are limited in number and have been extracted from their production and distribution contexts. Placed on different shelves, which are themselves situated in different sections of the store, supermarket products are associated, grouped, or dispersed in different ways. References and markings must allow consumers to classify products and make selections, choices (that are in part) qualculated by the intense activity of marketing professionals. To say that the supermarket is a qualculation space is not to say the space is homogeneous or that the qualculation is clear-cut and simple. The supermarket is in fact a space within which other qualculation devices abound: packaging, shopping lists, shopping carts allowing prior choices to be assessed at a glance, cash registers assigning numbers, and so on.
Different devices cohabit, fit together, are complementary to one another, or on the contrary, cancel each other out.
没有这些物质操作及其所需的装置，任何判断、任何计算都不可能进行。

质算的配置多种多样。电子证券交易所的订单簿是一个质算空间（字面意义上位于计算机内存之中），买入与卖出订单按照一套优先规则在其中得到排序。交易者可以在屏幕上观察订单簿，探究其深度，并以多种方式介入。执行价格由算法质算得出。超市也可以被视为一种质算装置。它所陈列的产品数量有限，并且已被从其生产与分销情境中抽离出来。超市产品被放置在不同的货架上，而这些货架本身又位于商店的不同区域，它们由此以不同方式被关联、归组或分散。商品参照信息与标识必须让消费者能够对产品进行分类并作出选择，而这些选择（部分地）是由营销专业人士的高强度活动质算出来的。说超市是一个质算空间，并不意味着这个空间是同质的，也不意味着质算是界限分明而简单的。事实上，超市是一个充斥着其他质算装置的空间：包装、购物清单、让人一眼就能评估先前选择的购物车、赋予数字的收银机，等等。
不同的装置共处、嵌合、彼此互补，或者相反，相互抵消。

One of the main advantages of this definition is that it connects the material and cognitive dimensions of qualculation. In other words, because it creates a space that allows for cognitive operations, qualculation cannot be carried through to an endpoint without mobilizing tools and equipment. The skills that agents must mobilize (identifying entities, constituting lists, establishing classifications, making hierarchies, writing reports) require specific extrasomatic resources. The set of specifications that prostheses and equipment must satisfy is strictly determined by the nature and purpose of the qualculative operations.
这一定义的主要优势之一，在于它把质算的物质维度与认知维度联系起来。换句话说，由于质算创造了一个容许认知操作的空间，若不调动工具与装备，质算便无法推进到终点。行动者必须调动的技能（识别实体、构成清单、建立分类、制定等级、撰写报告）需要特定的体外资源。义肢与装备必须满足的一整套规格，严格地由质算操作的性质与目的所决定。

Qualculation is first and foremost a material activity, even and especially when it is described as mental. This fact explains why evaluation operations cannot be dissociated from the process through which goods are qualified and requalified. Defined in this way, a process of evaluation does not remain external to the goods to which it is applied. The operations transform the goods. Each new qualculation, going through operations that identify, detach, put into relation, rank, and digitalize, requires a series of material and equipped operations based on dissociations, displacements, and reassociations. By that very fact, it modifies the entities on which it operates and restructures the spaces in which they move. This applies in a spectacular way to marketing activities, as we saw in the examples given to illustrate qualculation, but in an even more obvious and striking way, it applies to design and manufacture, and further downstream, to activities associated with usages. The process of transformation through evaluation acts on goods by reconfiguring the relations into which they enter and continues uninterrupted throughout the good’s career. Some measure of the scope and depth of transformation can be found by comparing the qualities of a good when it initially emerges in a still inchoate form from an R&D lab and the qualities that disappear with it when it is finally incinerated as waste.

质算首先而且首要是一种物质活动，即便、尤其是当它被描述为心智活动时也是如此。这一事实解释了为什么评估操作无法与物品被品质界定和重新界定品质的过程相分离。如此定义的评估过程，并不停留在其所适用的物品之外。这些操作会转化物品。每一次新的质算，都要经历识别、脱离、建立联系、排序和数字化等操作，因而需要一系列以分离、位移和重新关联为基础、并且配备装备的物质操作。正因如此，它改变了其所操作的实体，并重构了这些实体在其中运动的空间。这一点以引人注目的方式适用于营销活动，正如我们为说明质算而举的例子所示；但它以更为明显、更为醒目的方式适用于设计与制造，并进一步向下游适用于与使用相关的活动。经由评估而进行的转化过程，通过重构物品所进入的关系而作用于物品，并在物品的整个生涯中不间断地持续。只要比较一件物品最初以尚不清晰的形态从研发实验室中出现时的品质，与它最终作为废物被焚烧时随之消失的品质，便可在某种程度上衡量这种转化的范围与深度。

To offer a better grasp of the profound nature of the space-time described by his theory of relativity, Einstein imagined an experiment in which he rode a light wave. What could one learn and what could one see, he asked, if one were a proton, moving at the speed of light? Inspired by this thought experiment, one could decide to follow some cells from the moment they are manipulated in a petri dish by a researcher until their injection into a sick body. Those cells, after an itinerary from manipulation to manipulation, qualification to requalification, will allow a sick organ to regain some of its functions. Anyone given the chance to join these cells in their wanderings and reconfigurations would move with them from site to site, observing the evaluation operations different agents implement along the way. They would have a live experience of the successive transformations that result. Live observation makes clear why it is incorrect to restrict the term “production” to the manufacturing phase. A good is produced progressively, over its whole lifespan. It is production that transforms a cell, initially pluripotent, into a complex treatment dedicated to repairing the myocardium. What is true of a reprogrammed and reconfigured cell is equally true of any other good. Production of a car begins in a design department or in conception software; it continues on the platform on which the prototype is made, then in the manufacturing unit of factories, and finally in the dealer’s showroom. Production involves pushing an entity forward, displacing it from site to site while transforming and requalifying it in order to finally reach the bilateral transaction.

为了更好地把握其相对论所描述的时空的深刻本质，爱因斯坦（Albert Einstein）设想了一个实验：他骑在一道光波上。他问道，如果一个人是一个以光速运动的光子，他能了解到什么，又能看到什么？受这一思想实验启发，人们可以决定跟踪一些细胞，从研究人员在培养皿中操纵它们之时起，直到它们被注入一个患病的身体。这些细胞在经历从一个操作到另一个操作、从一次品质界定到另一次重新界定品质的行程之后，将使一个患病的器官恢复部分功能。任何有机会伴随这些细胞一同漫游、一同经历重新配置的人，都会随它们从一个场所迁移到另一个场所，观察不同行动者沿途实施的评估操作。他们将亲身经历由此产生的接连不断的转化。亲身观察清楚表明，为什么把“生产”一词局限于制造阶段是不正确的。一件物品是在其整个生命周期中逐步被生产出来的。正是生产把一个最初具有多能性的细胞转化为一种专用于修复心肌的复杂疗法。对经过重新编程和重新配置的细胞而言为真的事情，对任何其他物品同样为真。汽车的生产始于设计部门或概念设计软件；它继续于制作原型的平台上，继而继续于工厂的制造单元中，最后继续于经销商的展厅里。生产意味着推动一个实体向前，把它从一个场所移置到另一个场所，同时转化它、重新界定其品质，以便最终达成双边交易。

The term “qualculation” does not merely refer to the different material and cognitive, quantitative and qualitative operations through which properly equipped agents evaluate goods. It also refers to the fact that the evaluation, through its practical modalities, transforms and requalifies goods, fully participating in the process of their production. To evaluate is to qualculate; to qualculate is to requalify; to requalify is to produce.
“质算”一词不仅指装备齐备的行动者借以评估物品的各种物质与认知、定量与定性操作。它还指这样一个事实：评估通过其实践方式转化并重新界定物品的品质，从而充分参与物品的生产过程。评估就是质算；质算就是重新界定品质；重新界定品质就是生产。
You now know enough about evaluation as qualculation for me to introduce the notion of a
qualculative agency
现在，对于作为质算的评估，你已了解得足够多，我可以引入“质算能动者”（
qualculative agency
）这一概念了。
QUALCULATIVE AGENCIES
质算能动者

As I have just defined them, qualculations are materially cumbersome and involve complicated operations. Because of this complexity, the forces required to implement and discipline them go well beyond the capacities of a human brain or body. Instances of evaluation are made up of assemblages, collectives composed of technical elements, algorithms, cooperating human beings, procedures, and more. To mark this collective and heterogeneous dimension of qualculation, I choose to speak of “agencies” and not “agents.” Although the two words have differing etymologies, because of their homophony, the former is often substituted for the latter in usual usage. Like agents, an agency acts — it acts in a structuring and structured way. Like agents, an agency is capable of reflection, analysis, and strategic behavior, and like agents, it collects and makes collections, institutes differences, compares, classifies. An agency is capable of all that and therefore of qualculating because it is composed of a slew of human and nonhuman entities, both textual and material, that are solicited, that take initiatives, that cooperate to make it act. In a sense, the agency acts in the name of agents. This is easier to understand when the agency designates an explicitly collective entity, such as a company, an administration, a union, or a user group. It is also the case, however, when the agency works on behalf of an individual agent, such as a consumer, a trader, or a sales representative, who, as we will see, is heavily equipped and never acts or thinks alone.

正如我刚刚界定的，质算在物质上颇为笨重，并涉及复杂的操作。由于这种复杂性，实施质算并对其加以规训所需的力量，远远超出人的大脑或身体的能力。承担评估的单位由拼装体组成，即由技术要素、算法、合作的人、程序等构成的集体。为了标示质算的这一集体性、异质性维度，我选择说“能动者”（agencies）而非“行动者”（agents）。这两个词词源不同，但由于读音相同，在日常用法中前者常被用来替代后者。与行动者一样，能动者行动——它以既塑造结构、又受结构塑造的方式行动。与行动者一样，能动者能够反思、分析并采取策略行为；与行动者一样，它收集并制作集合、确立差异、比较、分类。能动者之所以能够做到这一切，因而能够进行质算，是因为它由大量人与非人实体构成，这些实体既有文本性的也有物质性的，它们被征召、采取主动、相互合作，使能动者得以行动。在某种意义上，能动者以行动者的名义行动。当能动者指一个明确集体性的实体——如公司、行政机构、工会或用户群体——时，这一点较易理解。然而，当能动者代表某个个体行动者——如消费者、交易员或销售代表——行事时，情况同样如此；我们将会看到，这样的个体行动者装备精良，从不独自行动或思考。

Each agency has capacities for qualculation, skills that are at least in part singular and original. This does not preclude that agencies may have some similar equipment or that there be family resemblances between them. Monsanto is as different as possible from Toyota, but from the point of view of an American pension fund that is looking for the best investment and that has adopted appropriate tools, comparisons between the two giant multinationals are possible and can be qualculated! A consumer in South Korea and one in Germany do not qualculate in exactly the same way, yet they mobilize a great number of similar sociocognitive prostheses. Some are shared and stable, others evolve over time and are subject to constant bricolage. To grasp the diversity of qualculative agencies, one must therefore start with an analysis of their equipment and look into the modalities of their design, implementation, and dissemination.

每个能动者都具有质算能力，即至少部分独一而原创的技能。这并不排除不同能动者可能拥有某些相似的装备，或彼此之间存在家族相似。孟山都（Monsanto）与丰田（Toyota）的差异之大无以复加，但从一家美国养老基金的角度看——它寻求最佳投资，并采用了适当的工具——这两家巨型跨国公司之间的比较是可能的，而且可以进行质算！韩国消费者与德国消费者的质算方式并不完全相同，但他们调用了大量相似的社会认知义肢。有些义肢是共享而稳定的，另一些则随时间演化，不断经历修补拼装（bricolage）。因此，要把握质算能动者的多样性，就必须从分析其装备入手，并考察其设计、实施与传播的方式。

Before jumping into the colorful world of agencies and their constitutive prostheses, I would like to reinforce an essential point I have already raised. A qualculative agency does not confront entities that are external to itself (that is, the goods in their different states). In qualculating, agencies intervene directly, through their equipment, to fashion the reality they evaluate. In sum, the equipped qualculation participates in instituting a reality that it contributes to making exist, and it makes obsolete the stark opposition between a subject who evaluates and an evaluated object.
在跳入能动者及其构成性义肢的五彩世界之前，我想强调一个已经提出的要点。质算能动者并不面对外在于自身的实体（即处于不同状态的物品）。在质算时，能动者通过其装备直接介入，塑造它们所评估的现实。总之，装备齐备的质算参与创设一种现实，而它本身也促成了这种现实的存在，并使“进行评估的主体”与“被评估的客体”之间那种截然对立变得过时。

To make this point very clear, let us return to the one piece of equipment that has profoundly shaped modern commercial activities and is at the heart of the form of market economy that is called capitalism. Not all markets are capitalist — it should be clear by now that this hypothesis guides my investigations. But those that are can be identified by their qualculative tools, and in particular because they mobilize an accounting tool: double-entry bookkeeping. Tell me how you qualculate, and I will tell you how much of a capitalist you are.
为了把这一点讲清楚，让我们回到一件深刻塑造了现代商业活动、并处于所谓资本主义市场经济形式之核心的装备。并非所有市场都是资本主义的——至此应当清楚，这一假设指导着我的研究。但那些资本主义市场可以通过其质算工具来识别，尤其因为它们调用了一种会计工具：复式记账。告诉我你如何质算，我就能说出你在多大程度上是个资本主义者。

Max Weber devoted a significant part of his energies to answering a simple question: Why did capitalism develop in the West at the turn of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries? His answer invokes two main and complementary factors. The first is the Protestant ethic. The second, which later gave rise to numerous studies, but is less well known, involves the invention and especially the widespread diffusion and implementation of double-entry bookkeeping. Double-entry bookkeeping is an accounting tool that ensures that all realized operations are doubly registered, once as credit and once as debit. It allows one to follow the value of the assets an agent accumulates and to measure what are now called returns on investment. In sum, capitalism, in order to develop as we know it, needed a spirit to guide it and a tool of control to keep it on course. The spirit was provided by religion, the control by the Venetian banks of the fifteenth century. The spirit orients the action, the tool checks that the sought-after results are obtained and can influence the action, should that prove necessary.

马克斯·韦伯（Max Weber）把相当一部分精力用于回答一个简单问题：为什么资本主义在17、18世纪之交的西方发展起来？他的答案援引两个主要且互补的因素。第一个是新教伦理。第二个后来引发了大量研究，但较少为人所知，涉及复式记账的发明，尤其是其广泛传播与实施。复式记账是一种会计工具，确保所有已发生的业务都被双重登记，一次记为贷方，一次记为借方。它使人能够追踪行动者所积累资产的价值，并衡量如今所谓的投资回报。总之，资本主义要按其为人所知的样子发展，既需要一种精神来引导它，也需要一种控制工具使它不偏离轨道。精神由宗教提供，控制则由15世纪的威尼斯银行提供。精神为行动定向，工具则核查所追求的结果是否达成，并在必要时影响行动。

This linkage of the spirit and the tools of capitalism, which Weber implicitly refuses, is very suggestive. Yet it is laden with ambiguities, compatible with two opposite interpretations, each of which claims to explain why the agent is pushed to accumulate capital in view of drawing the highest possible revenue from it. According to the first interpretation, control of the operations is in the agent’s hands: he is the pilot and the only pilot. Double-entry bookkeeping provides the tool he needs to implement his programs and check that he reaches his objectives. The spirit of capitalism that animates agents has at its disposal an instrument that allows it to check its own direction. The second interpretation defends the opposite thesis. Double-entry bookkeeping, by the simple fact of being used, imposes a logical, qualculative coherence on agents that goes well beyond what they would be capable of if left to their own devices. Without double-entry bookkeeping, no agent would be in a position to become a capitalist, attentive to accumulation and returns on investment. In one case, the tool is completely controlled; in the other, it relentlessly dictates its law.

这种把资本主义的精神与工具联系起来的做法，虽为韦伯暗中拒绝，却极富启发性。然而它充满歧义，可以容纳两种相反的解释，二者都声称能说明为什么行动者会被推动去积累资本，以便从中获取尽可能高的收益。按照第一种解释，对各项操作的控制掌握在行动者手中：他是驾驶员，而且是唯一的驾驶员。复式记账提供了他实施计划、核查自己是否达到目标所需的工具。驱动行动者的资本主义精神，拥有一种可以核查自身方向的工具。第二种解释则主张相反的论点。复式记账仅仅因为被使用，就把一种逻辑上、质算上的连贯性强加给行动者，这种连贯性远远超出他们若自行其是所能达到的程度。没有复式记账，任何行动者都不可能成为资本主义者，不可能关注积累与投资回报。在一种情况下，工具被完全控制；在另一种情况下，工具无情地颁布自己的法则。

Until recently, it was not possible to move beyond this opposition and the endless controversies surrounding double-entry bookkeeping. There are those who, following in Werner Sombart’s steps, consider it to be the moving force of capitalism and others who assert that without the help of a true entrepreneurial spirit, rooted in mentalities, a mere accounting tool could not have led to the rise of capitalism. It is not the double accounting that calculates, they add, but rather the human agent, the entrepreneur who uses it. In one case, the agent does what the tool prescribes; in the other, he conceives of the tools that improve what he wants to do.

直到不久以前，人们还无法超越这一对立以及围绕复式记账的无休止争论。有些人追随维尔纳·桑巴特（Werner Sombart）的脚步，认为复式记账是资本主义的动力；另一些人则断言，若没有一种植根于心态之中的真正企业家精神的帮助，单纯的会计工具不可能导致资本主义的兴起。他们还说，进行计算的不是复式记账，而是使用它的人类行动者，即企业家。在一种情况下，行动者做工具所规定的事；在另一种情况下，他构想出能够改进自己想做之事的工具。

Studies devoted to accounting techniques and management tools over the last few decades provide a way out of this sterile controversy by showing that both theses are as false as they are true. An entrepreneur who calculates his profits and measures the accumulation of his capital does not use double- entry bookkeeping in order to make a more precise, rapid, and exact calculation, the idea of which would have preexisted the tool itself. Nor does he let himself be blindly led by the tool. It is the duo made up of the entrepreneur and the double-entry bookkeeping that conceives of the calculation and executes it. One might even say that double-entry bookkeeping, by the mere fact of its availability, suggests the calculation to the entrepreneur, who, in return, accepts the invitation and asks double-entry bookkeeping to make the calculation it offers while being ready also to modify the tool if the latter does not prove entirely satisfactory.

The relations between the elements of this duo, the agent and the double-entry bookkeeping, are complex. Each element suggests and stimulates the other. Double-entry bookkeeping does not measure an accumulation of capital that developed without it and to which it gives the instruments it needs. Rather — Weber says it explicitly — it contributes to establishing or instituting the very accumulation it measures: “Capital accounting,” without which there would be no talk of accumulation, “is the valuation and verification of opportunities for profit and of the success of profit-making activity by means of a valuation of the total assets (goods and money) of the enterprise at the beginning of a profit-making venture, and the comparison of this with a similar valuation of the assets still present and newly acquired, at the end of the process.” Weber adds that this capital account does not observe practices, but rather establishes what he calls lucrative activities: “An economic ‘enterprise’ [
Unternehmen

] is autonomous action capable of orientation to capital accounting. This orientation takes place by means of ‘calculation’; ex-ante calculation of the probable risks and chances of profit, ex-post calculation for the verification of the actual profit or loss resulting.”

过去几十年关于会计技术与管理工具的研究，为摆脱这场无结果的争论提供了出路：这些研究表明，两种论点既同样错误，也同样正确。一个计算利润、衡量资本积累的企业家，使用复式记账并不是为了进行一种更精确、更迅速、更准确的计算——仿佛这种计算的观念早在工具之前就已存在。他也不会让自己被工具盲目牵着走。构想并执行计算的，是由企业家与复式记账共同组成的二人组。甚至可以说，复式记账仅仅因为可供使用，就向企业家提示了这种计算；企业家则接受邀请，要求复式记账完成它所提供的计算，同时也准备在工具不能完全令人满意时修改工具。

这个二人组内部各要素——行动者与复式记账——之间的关系十分复杂。每个要素都提示并刺激另一个要素。复式记账并不是在衡量一种在没有它的情况下发展起来、而它为之提供必要工具的资本积累。相反——韦伯明确这样说——它参与确立或创设它所要衡量的那种积累本身：“资本会计”——没有它，就无从谈论积累——“是通过对营利事业开始时企业全部资产（物品与货币）的估价，并把这一估价与过程结束时仍然存在和新取得的资产的类似估价相比较，来评估和核查营利机会以及营利活动是否成功。”韦伯还补充说，这种资本账目并不观察实践，而是确立他所谓的营利活动：“一个经济‘企业’［
Unternehmen
］是能够以资本会计为取向的自主行动。这种取向通过‘计算’进行；事前计算可能的风险与营利机会，事后计算则核查由此产生的实际利润或亏损。”
A capital account orients the action and makes the agent a potential capitalist, who, by endorsing the tool, becomes an acting capitalist.
资本账目为行动定向，使行动者成为潜在的资本主义者；行动者一旦认可这一工具，便成为行动中的资本主义者。

As Ève Chiapello emphasizes, in order even to speak of accumulation and returns on capital, one must have at one’s disposal the very notion of capital, which we now recognize is the result of identifiable operations established and described by accounting institutions. One must also be able to grasp and measure how it increases as it circulates and goes through metamorphoses.

It is not an exaggeration to say that the categories that serve to think markets, to shape and frame commercial activity, are linked to the existence of the duo made up by human agents and accounting “tools.” This is true both of capitalist markets and of what are called “alternative” markets. In one case, there are capital accounts, in the other, accounting techniques that make things such as surplus production explicit, whose use can then be discussed by the parties involved.
正如埃娃·夏皮罗（Ève Chiapello）所强调的，要谈论积累与资本回报，首先必须掌握资本这一概念本身；我们现在认识到，这一概念是由会计机构确立并描述的、可识别的操作所产生的结果。人们还必须能够把握并衡量资本在流通、经历变形时如何增长。
可以毫不夸张地说，用来思考市场、塑造并框定商业活动的那些范畴，与由人的行动者和会计“工具”组成的二人组的存在相关联。这对资本主义市场以及所谓“替代性”市场都成立。在前一种情况下，有资本账目；在后一种情况下，则有一些会计技术，它们使剩余生产之类的东西变得明确，而其使用随后可以由相关各方讨论。

The duo of agents and their tools, or, if you prefer, tools and their agents, is like a pair of dancers who make each other dance as they dance themselves, leading or following depending on the moment, in such a way as to improvise and compose a choreography that, to the spectator, looks as though a single spirit has inspired it; in the same way, one speaks of the spirit of capitalism to refer to the partnership between the entrepreneur and his accounts. Take away either of the dancers, and the dance, like capitalism, vanishes like a dream.
行动者及其工具——或者，如果你愿意，也可以说工具及其行动者——组成的二人组，就像一对舞者：他们在自己起舞的同时也让对方起舞，时而领舞，时而跟随，即兴编排出一套舞蹈；在观众看来，这套舞蹈仿佛由同一种精神所激发。同样，人们谈论资本主义精神，指的正是企业家与其账目之间的伙伴关系。拿掉任何一个舞者，舞蹈就会像资本主义一样，如梦般消散。

This adjustment between two partners, an adjustment that ensures that they dance a tango as much as the tango makes them dance, is the result of a long history. The same goes for capitalism. As Peter Miller and later Ève Chiapello explain, notions such as capital, salary, profit, or return on investment, which serve as reference points for entrepreneurial (capitalist) action, were elaborated over long periods and in close interaction with the accounting practices that inform them. This story is now quite well known. Luca Pacioli, a student of Leon Battista Alberti’s, presents double-entry bookkeeping in its canonical form in 1494. By registering operations twice, it connects different accounts (debit/credit; liability/asset), presenting each of them on two juxtaposed pages so that one can see them at a single glance. This presentation (called “bilateral”) makes it possible to determine how much different lines of activity participate in profit making and to track how the profit evolves. It took time to unify and standardize this accounting tool. For a long time, the debit and credit accounts continued to be presented sequentially, rather than being juxtaposed. In the middle of the sixteenth century, Fugger, the famous banking family, had still not adopted the complete system. It would therefore be an exaggeration to claim that behavior as varied as maximizing profit or managing partnerships is a mechanical consequence of double-entry bookkeeping: double-entry bookkeeping becomes a universal technique only in the nineteenth century. As with any innovation, the adjustment process between tools and dispositions was a process drawn out through different variations, setbacks, or sudden advances, fought over by both pioneers and opponents. Capitalism took form with and through its accounting tools over the course of this mutual process of apprenticeship. Each one reshaped the other simultaneously.

两个伙伴之间的这种调适——它既确保他们跳一支探戈，也确保探戈使他们起舞——是漫长历史的结果。资本主义亦然。正如彼得·米勒（Peter Miller）以及后来的埃娃·夏皮罗所解释的，资本、工资、利润或投资回报等概念，作为企业家（资本主义）行动的参照点，是在漫长时期中、在与赋予它们内容的会计实践的密切互动中逐步形成的。这段历史如今已相当为人所知。莱昂·巴蒂斯塔·阿尔贝蒂（Leon Battista Alberti）的学生卢卡·帕乔利（Luca Pacioli）于1494年以典范形式介绍了复式记账。复式记账通过把交易登记两次，把不同账户（借方/贷方；负债/资产）连接起来，将每个账户呈现在并排的两页上，使人一眼便能看清。这种（被称为“双边”的）呈现方式，使人能够确定不同业务线在多大程度上参与营利，并追踪利润如何演变。统一并使这一会计工具标准化花了很长时间。在很长一段时期里，借方与贷方账户仍按先后顺序呈现，而非并排呈现。16世纪中叶，著名的银行家族富格尔（Fugger）仍未采用完整体系。因此，若断言最大化利润或管理合伙关系这类各异的行为是复式记账的机械后果，那就言过其实了：复式记账直到19世纪才成为一种普遍技术。与任何创新一样，工具与禀性之间的调适过程经历了各种变异、挫折或突进，被先驱与反对者争夺。资本主义在这一相互学习的过程中，与其会计工具一道、并通过其会计工具而形成。二者同时重塑了对方。

An agent who calculates his profits and the increase in his assets is an agent who is equipped. The key point to remember, however, is that the equipment is not composed of neutral instruments. Return on investment no more preexists in the agent’s mind than it exists objectively outside the agent. Return on investment is instituted by the calculations of an equipped agent, and its being instituted owes as much to the agent as to the equipment.
一个计算自身利润与资产增长的行动者，是一个装备齐备的行动者。然而要记住的关键点是，装备并非由中性的工具构成。投资回报并不先在地存在于行动者的心灵中，也并不客观地存在于行动者之外。投资回报是由装备齐备的行动者的计算所创设的，而它的被创设，既归功于行动者，也归功于装备。
This finding has a general value. Qualculative agencies, the name I give to these qualculating duos, contribute significantly to instituting the realities they qualculate.

Market shares, a juicy market sector such as those industrial activities described by employees of the Boston Consulting Group as “cash cows,” only take shape, can only be manipulated, and can only orient action, even as they are also the object of action through the marketing tools or the BCG studies that bring them into existence.

If you change the equipment, commercial practices undergo a deep transformation. Operations such as establishing lists, filling in Excel spreadsheets, setting up macros to multiply and add lines or columns, keeping books of accounts — all these put elements of material support into play. Their structuring power, however, goes much further. These operations are connected to a set of activities that are part of logistics in the traditional sense of the term and without which qualculations would be impossible. Manipulations in accounting correspond to operations and notions such as stock and storage, inventory and counting, shelf placement, packaging, or bar codes.
这一发现具有普遍价值。质算能动者——我以此称呼这些进行质算的二人组——对创设它们所质算的现实有重大贡献。
市场份额，以及诸如波士顿咨询公司（Boston Consulting Group）员工称为“现金牛”（cash cows）的那些工业活动所形成的油水丰厚的市场部门，只有通过使它们得以存在的营销工具或 BCG 研究，才得以成形、被操纵并为行动定向，同时也成为行动的对象。
如果你改变装备，商业实践就会经历深刻转变。开列清单、填写 Excel 表格、设置用于乘加行或列的宏、记账等操作，全都调动了物质支撑要素。然而，它们的结构化力量远不止于此。这些操作与一组活动相连，这些活动属于传统意义上的物流，没有它们，质算将不可能进行。会计中的操作对应着库存与仓储、盘点与计数、货架陈列、包装或条形码等操作与概念。
SOME EXAMPLES OF DIVERSE AGENCIES AND THEIR EQUIPMENT
多样能动者及其装备的若干示例

Qualculative agencies associated with the manufacturing, marketing, and consumer activities on the forefront of the commercial scene are highly visible. They should not, however, lead us to forget all the other agencies, those working in the shadows, those that interface markets tend to relegate to the margins, but that are nevertheless at the heart of market agencements. These agencies may belong to the world of design, or to the world of users, or to any one of the intermediary spheres that contribute to the uninterrupted chain of successive requalifications of goods.
与商业场景前沿的制造、营销和消费活动相关的质算能动者十分显眼。然而，它们不应使我们忘记所有其他能动者——那些在暗处工作的能动者，那些被界面市场倾向于排挤到边缘、却仍处于市场装配核心的能动者。这些能动者可能属于设计的世界，或用户的世界，或任何参与物品连续不断的品质重新界定链条的中间领域。

In this section, I would like to give some idea of just how diverse qualculative agencies are. First, I want to show that agencies are everywhere, profiling and classifying. I also want to highlight a number of unexplored terrains. Despite the efforts that have been made to delve into the universe of qualculative agencies, many sites, including strategic ones, have not yet been sufficiently studied. The idea that
there is no one best way to qualculate
commercial transactions optimally should emerge as we move through the section. This result will be essential to refresh the analysis of market efficiency. (See Chapter 8.)

并不存在唯一最佳方式来最优地质算商业交易
”这一观念应当逐渐浮现。这一结果对于刷新市场效率分析至关重要。（参见第八章。）

这些词无处不在。随便翻开一本消费者评测杂志——例如法国《选择》（
