The following examples do not claim to be exhaustive. They simply aim to suggest and illustrate the omnipresence of qualculating agencies and how diverse their skills are over the course of the passiva(c)tion process. For the most part, these agencies relate to market agencements’ areas that are upstream of commercial transactions. In a later section devoted to power relations, I will try to correct for this asymmetry by focusing on the agencies on the consumption side of the process.
以下例子并不自称详尽无遗。它们只想提示并例示质算能动者的无所不在，以及在整个被动化过程中它们的技能何其多样。这些能动者大多与市场装配中商业交易上游的领域相关。在随后专论权力关系的一节中，我将把注意力放在过程消费一侧的能动者上，以纠正这一不对称。
IN RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT

When I started my research career, at the beginning of the 1970s, it was not easy to persuade French companies to accept being studied by a sociologist who promised nothing in return. May ’68 was fresh in everyone’s memory, and no one had forgotten that the social sciences had played an active role in what were then called “the events.” Thanks to Lucien Karpik, then director of the Centre de sociologie de l’innovation, and on the recommendation of Pierre Laffitte, then director of the École des Mines, I had an opportunity to be integrated in a large French industrial group that was present on all continents and a leader in its field. My only mission was to understand how innovation projects were conceived and carried out. I was free to move around as I pleased — the doors were wide open. The only concession asked of me was that I introduce myself not as a sociologist, but as an engineer-sociologist. Within a few weeks everyone in fact forgot that I was a sociologist. That did not bother me at all, especially since I had a diploma as “Ingénieur des mines” and a masters and higher degree in economics in my pocket!
在研究与发展中

当我于20世纪70年代初开始研究生涯时，要说服法国企业接受一位不承诺任何回报的社会学家来研究它们并不容易。1968年五月事件在所有人记忆中仍很新鲜，没有人忘记社会科学在当时所谓的“事件”中扮演了积极角色。多亏时任创新社会学中心（Centre de sociologie de l’innovation）主任的吕西安·卡尔皮克（Lucien Karpik），以及时任矿业学院（École des Mines）院长皮埃尔·拉菲特（Pierre Laffitte）的推荐，我得以进入一家大型法国工业集团；该集团遍布各大洲，并在其领域居领先地位。我唯一的任务是理解创新项目如何被构想和执行。我可以随意走动——大门对我敞开。对我唯一的要求是作出一点让步：我介绍自己时不能说自己是社会学家，而要说自己是工程师—社会学家。几周之内，事实上所有人都忘了我是一个社会学家。我一点也不介意，尤其因为我口袋里装着“矿业工程师”（Ingénieur des mines）文凭以及经济学硕士和高等学位证书！

After a few months, having visited the groups’ different centers and research labs and having interviewed dozens of those who worked in the research, production, and marketing departments, I had acquired a solid understanding of the innovation projects under way. I was just a young engineer who seemed to have been given a vague evaluation assignment by the management. Without a doubt, this is why the director of R&D asked me to test a tool that had been recommended to him by a consulting firm. To be applied, this very simple instrument required that a list of the research and innovation projects be established. I quickly realized that my role was not so much to identify the projects as to constitute them from a scattered group of operations among which I was to try to find some coherence. Once this list was obtained . . . and approved . . . the following step involved imagining a set of criteria through which projects could be grouped in homogeneous categories. I was not terribly imaginative in the criteria I suggested for classifying projects: aims (knowledge acquisition, development, product innovation, process innovation, and so on), forms of organization (one or several centers involved, subcontracting to outside organizations), budget, and more.

几个月后，在走访了该集团的不同中心和实验室、并访谈了数十位在研究、生产和营销部门工作的人之后，我已对进行中的创新项目有了扎实的了解。我只是一个年轻工程师，似乎被管理层赋予了一项模糊的评估任务。无疑正因如此，研发总监让我测试一家咨询公司推荐给他的工具。这一非常简单的工具若要付诸应用，需要先建立一份研究与创新项目清单。我很快意识到，我的角色与其说是识别项目，不如说是从一组零散的操作中把它们构成出来，并设法在这些操作之间找到某种连贯性。清单一旦获得……并获得批准……下一步就是设想一套标准，据此把项目归入同质的类别。我为项目分类提出的标准并不算很有想象力：目标（知识获取、开发、产品创新、流程创新等）、组织形式（涉及一个或多个中心、外包给外部组织）、预算等等。

The next step was to situate the projects in a hierarchy, to produce hierarchies not only within each class, but also between classes. The consulting company, which had made an inventory of practices in use in the industrial world, suggested using qualiquantitative formulas; I shamelessly adopted and adapted them. These formulas, which link a certain number of parameters such as the cost of a project, its duration, number of researchers involved, market share anticipated, and so on, also included a scientific appreciation in the form of a score from 1 to 5 on the basis of a few subcriteria. I had been told that this score should be taken very seriously because the long-term quality of the group’s R&D depended on it. I therefore spent hours with the scientific director, an eminent scientist, and some of his colleagues, “grading” the scientific quality of projects. After many hours of investigation and interviews, I had in hand a table that presented all of the projects and their different scores.

下一步是把项目排入等级，不仅要在每个类别内部、而且要在类别之间建立等级。那家咨询公司曾对工业界通行的做法作过盘点，它建议使用定性与定量相结合的公式；我毫无愧色地采用了这些公式并加以改造。这些公式把若干参数——如项目成本、持续时间、参与研究人员数量、预期市场份额等——联系起来，还包括一项科学评价，即依据若干子标准给出1至5分的评分。有人告诉我，这个分数必须认真对待，因为集团研发的长期质量取决于它。于是，我与科研总监——一位杰出科学家——及其几位同事花了数小时，为项目的科学质量“打分”。经过许多小时的调查和访谈，我手中得到了一张表格，列出了所有项目及其各项分数。

When I finished this task, I had a confused feeling, sharpened by a touch of guilty conscience, that the result was arbitrary, that the ranking was nonsense — as engineers like to say, believing only their lab instruments, which spit out numbers that do not react to the experimenter’s mood swings. Start the procedure all over again with the same projects, and you will end up with a completely different result! What reassured me at the time was that deep down, I was convinced that all the tables I had filled in would end up abandoned in a cupboard to the gnawing criticism of mice. I was convinced that the various interests and power relations would continue to determine the decisions concerning the funding of the projects. What I did not immediately understand, but realized when a few months later the director of R&D invited me to an executive committee meeting, was that the famous scientific score that had required so much work was going to make it possible to save some projects that would otherwise have completely disappeared, so far did they appear to be from the market! Of course, the tool had not abolished influence relations — the meeting gave me a chance to see just how violent they could be — but it did participate in their reconfiguration. A scientific director who can show a score that guarantees a project’s contribution to the long-term future and to the company’s reputation has a far greater chance of making himself heard.

完成这项任务时，我有一种含混的感觉，这种感觉又因一丝负罪感而更加尖锐：结果是任意的，排序毫无意义——就像工程师们爱说的那样，他们只相信实验室仪器，因为仪器吐出的数字不会随实验者的情绪波动而变。用同样的项目把程序重来一遍，你会得到完全不同的结果！当时让我安心的是，我内心深处相信，我填过的所有表格最终都会被丢进柜子，任凭老鼠啃噬和批评。我相信，各种利益与权力关系将继续决定有关项目资助的决定。我当时没有立刻明白、但几个月后研发总监邀请我参加执行委员会会议时才发现的是：那个耗费了如此多心血的著名科学评分，将使一些否则会完全消失的项目得以保存下来——它们看起来离市场实在太远了！当然，工具并没有废除影响力关系——那次会议让我有机会看到这些关系可能多么粗暴——但它确实参与了这些关系的重新配置。一位科研总监若能出示一个分数，证明某项目对公司的长远未来和声誉有所贡献，他让别人听见自己意见的机会就大得多。

Once my assignment was finished, I did what I should have done before I started. I rushed to the (numerous) books and reports on selection tools for industrial innovation projects. I realized that my work fell within a wider move to design and formalize qualculation tools for research and innovation activities. Like the one I had helped to design and set up, scrupulously following the instructions I had been given, all these tools have analogous characteristics: they establish lists of projects, group them into classes, give them a score in order to be able, in the end, to constitute what was beginning to be called a portfolio of R&D activities. The techniques for constituting projects and the procedures for classifying and grading vary from one method to another. However, as was easily verified, in all cases, by participating in their characterization, evaluation, and hierarchical ranking, these tools contributed to shaping and transforming the research and innovation activities themselves. Of course, these qualculating activities did not appear out of nowhere. In one way or another, often implicitly, they already existed, but the equipment they had was different, and it therefore oriented and shaped the activities differently. The qualculative agency has been transformed by the systematic use of formalized tools and their gradual transformations. The scientific score has become less important, and with this modification of the qualculation tool, R&D has been massively reoriented toward more short-term projects or projects with a closer connection to markets as they can be anticipated,
redefining the
profiling
of research and the ways in which goods that will get as far as the market are qualified. Change the qualculation tool, transform the qualculative agency, and you get different goods.

任务完成后，我做了本该在开始前就做的事。我赶紧去读关于工业创新项目筛选工具的大量书籍和报告。我意识到，我的工作属于一个更广泛的进程：为研究与创新活动设计并形式化质算工具。与我所参与设计并严格按照所获指示建立的那套工具一样，所有这些工具都有类似特征：它们建立项目清单，把项目归入类别，给项目打分，以便最终构成当时开始被称为研发活动“组合”（portfolio）的东西。构成项目的技术，以及分类与分级的程序，因方法而异。然而，正如人们容易验证的那样，在所有这些案例中，这些工具通过参与项目的
特征刻画
、评估和等级排序，促成了研究与创新活动本身的塑造与转化。当然，这些质算活动并非凭空出现。它们以某种方式、往往是隐含地早已存在，但当时所拥有的装备不同，因此以不同方式为活动定向并塑造活动。质算能动者因形式化工具的系统使用及其逐渐变化而被转化。科学评分变得不那么重要；随着质算工具的这一改变，研发被大规模地重新导向更短期的项目，或与可预期的市场联系更紧密的项目，
从而重新界定了研究的画像，也重新界定了那些终将抵达市场的物品被品质界定的方式。改变质算工具，转化质算能动者，你就会得到不同的物品。

What is particularly interesting in the case of R&D is the inverse relation between the evanescent nature of the activities to be evaluated and the arsenal of tools and instruments implemented to evaluate them. When entities are harder to identify, collect, group into homogeneous classes, compare, and rank, the heavier and more complex the equipment becomes. To give an image in a slightly different vocabulary from the one I am using here: uncertainties about the qualities of a good do not discourage qualculation; on the contrary they make it ever more necessary and more sophisticated.
在研发案例中特别有趣的是，待评估活动的转瞬即逝性与用于评估它们的工具和仪器库之间存在反向关系。当实体更难被识别、收集、归入同质类别、比较和排序时，装备就变得越笨重、越复杂。用一个与我此处略有不同的词汇来说：物品品质的不确定性并不使质算望而却步；相反，它使质算越发必要、越发精巧。
IN START-UPS

As the passiva(c)tion process grows longer, an increasing number of agencies intervene in the process, providing plenty of illustrations that the more uncertain a good is, the more it requires qualculation and sophisticated equipment. Since the beginning of the 1970s, for instance, formalized qualculation equipment has intruded into all the activities involved in designing and developing goods. Designing equipment has become more difficult and more problematic because the way these activities are organized has changed profoundly over the last two decades. Big companies, which used to prefer doing their research internally, tend now to outsource it. This change is particularly noticeable in the health sector. “Big Pharma” companies such as Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline, Novartis, or Sanofi take over developing and commercializing promising molecules while delegating the conception of such molecules to contract research organizations or very innovative small companies, biotech start-ups, which they reserve the right to buy out.
在初创企业中

随着被动化过程变得更长，越来越多的能动者介入其中，充分说明物品越不确定，就越需要质算和精巧的装备。例如，自20世纪70年代初以来，形式化的质算装备已侵入设计、开发物品所涉及的一切活动。设计装备变得更加困难、更加棘手，因为这些活动的组织方式在过去二十年里发生了深刻变化。过去倾向于在内部进行研究的大公司，如今往往将其外包。这一变化在医疗健康领域尤为明显。辉瑞（Pfizer）、葛兰素史克（GlaxoSmithKline）、诺华（Novartis）或赛诺菲（Sanofi）等“大型制药公司”（Big Pharma）接手有前景分子的开发与商业化，而把这类分子的构想委托给合同研究组织或极具创新性的小型公司——生物技术初创企业，并保留收购这些企业的权利。

The choice to outsource research makes qualculations devilishly complicated. On the one hand, there are the start-ups that do the initial development of molecules and vectors while these are still very far from constituting medical treatments and will require numerous qualifications, requalifications, and transformations before they can be prescribed by a general practitioner or a hospital and be covered by medical insurers. On the other hand, there are the Big Pharmas, seeking new molecules and ready for the long uphill battle to gain approval for commercialization, even if it is extremely expensive, because in the current economic system, it can provide huge returns. However, before deciding to take the plunge, the Big Pharma company has to have answers to some simple questions: Is there a chance that these molecules will lead to a profitable therapy? Will it be possible to replace the test subjects with real patients? Will the researchers be able to hand this over to doctors? In other words, how can the molecules be evaluated — that is to say, how can their current qualities be defined while anticipating their future qualities? How can one undertake to evaluate a molecule whose chances of success are often meager and whose commercial potential, expressed in sales revenues, will be known only a decade later, once it has gone through a complete cycle of transformations?

把研究外包的选择使质算变得异常复杂。一方面，初创企业进行分子与载体的初步开发，而这些分子与载体距离构成医疗手段还很远，需要经过大量品质界定、重新界定品质和转化，才能由全科医生或医院开出，并由医疗保险公司承保。另一方面，大型制药公司寻求新分子，并准备为获得商业化批准而进行漫长而艰难的斗争，即使代价极其高昂，因为在当前经济体制中，这可能带来巨额回报。然而，在决定冒险投入之前，大型制药公司必须回答一些简单问题：这些分子是否有望成为有利可图的疗法？是否有可能用真实患者取代试验对象？研究人员能否把成果交给医生？换言之，如何评估这些分子——也就是说，如何在预见其未来品质的同时界定其当前品质？如何着手评估一个成功率往往很低、其商业潜力（以销售收入衡量）只有在十年之后、经过一整轮转化才能为人所知的分子？
Rather than imagine a theoretical and abstract answer to these questions, Liliana Doganova went to the field to investigate.

She discovered the central role played by what the natives call “business models,” not to be confused with “business plans.” The business plan comes later, after the business model, once the qualities of the goods that are candidates for commercialization have been determined more precisely and it becomes possible to do market surveys, analyze the competition, estimate sales, and so on. The molecule that is still in the lab state is too uncertain, too unpredictable, to submit to those sorts of exercises. Yet that is not a reason to give up or hand things over to simple judgment or mere intuition. Of course, we already know that purely numerical calculation is impossible. Frank Knight was right: when the event or the entity to be calculated has no precedent, when it is unique and moreover is in a transitory state, a numerical calculation on the basis of objective or subjective probabilities cannot be made.
However, as the business model proves, qualculation is conceivable.
莉莉安娜·多甘诺娃（Liliana Doganova）没有为这些问题设想理论性的抽象答案，而是到实地进行调查。

她发现，当地人所称的“商业模式”（business model）发挥着核心作用；不可把它与“商业计划书”（business plan）混为一谈。商业计划书出现得较晚，在商业模式之后；此时候选商业化的物品之品质已被更精确地界定，因而有可能进行市场调查、分析竞争、估算销售额等。仍处于实验室状态的分子太不确定、太不可预测，无法承受这类操作。然而，这并非放弃、或把事情交给简单判断或纯粹直觉的理由。当然，我们已经知道，纯数值计算是不可能的。弗兰克·奈特（Frank Knight）说得对：当待计算的事件或实体没有先例，当它是独一的、并且处于过渡状态时，就不可能依据客观或主观概率进行数值计算。
然而，正如商业模式所证明的，质算是可以设想的。

The only way to get started is to dismiss the supposed uniqueness of the molecule being considered and to seek out its fellow creatures by exploring databases or searching available memories. As Doganova and Marie Eyquem-Renault tell us, there is no more violent obsession than the one that impels agencies to identify similar goods when they are dealing with novel, singular beings that may seem unique, but that never arrive alone and isolated in a brand new world. Compare! That is the injunction. And to succeed in that requires unbridled imagination, endless investigations, testing relationships, consulting huge databases, summoning consultants and experts who have been living among such molecules for years. When the investigation is concluded, while the singularity of the molecule in question has been preserved (since that is where its value lies), it is no longer alone. With a little elbowing, it has been pushed into classifications, networks of chemical, biological, social, regulatory, and financial relations, and it is inscribed in rankings. Its capacities have been clarified, and it begins to inhabit a familiar world populated by beings that are expected to treat identified pathologies more or less well. As a consequence of those abilities, through good times and bad, probabilities can be associated with these molecules in ways that are neither purely subjective (because they are the result of lengthy ordering labor) nor purely objective (this ordering is hypothetical), but that do lead to rankings, ordinal scales, and with a little insistence, cardinal scales! One can thus compare estimations and chances, getting around the problem Knight correctly identified. And from this emerges a first version of a business model, subject of course to requalculation, whose only aim is not to calculate yields or returns on investment, but to show that value can be created; the business model can qualculate molecules in order to say to what extent, appropriately pass(act)ivated, they will be in a position to attach themselves to a sick, suffering body. To show how generalized this tool is and that the qualculation made by Big Pharmas and biotechs is not out of the ordinary, Doganova observes that the practices through which the relations and evaluations are construed can be analyzed with the same notions anthropologist Jane Guyer put forward to describe African markets: naming, listing, classifying, comparing, establishing hierarchies, and finally attributing scores.
Nihil novum sub sole

— there’s nothing new under the sun. It is not that nothing new ever happens — this molecule is unique — but more simply, that nothing is so new that it cannot be qualculated by properly equipped agencies. The water Heraclitus watched flow is never the same, but it is always water.

要开始，唯一的办法是抛弃所考虑分子的所谓独一性，通过探索数据库或检索可用的记忆，去寻找它的同类。正如多甘诺娃与玛丽·艾克姆-雷诺（Marie Eyquem-Renault）告诉我们的，再没有比这更强烈的执念了：当能动者面对新奇的独一存在者——它们看似独一无二，却从不孤立地、独自地来到一个全新世界——时，这种执念驱使他们去识别相似的物品。比较！这就是命令。而要成功做到这一点，需要无拘无束的想象力、无休止的调查、检验关系、查询庞大的数据库、召来那些多年来与这类分子朝夕相处的顾问和专家。调查结束时，所涉分子的独一性得到了保留（因为价值正在于此），但它不再孤立。经过一番推挤，它被推进分类体系，推进由化学、生物、社会、监管与金融关系构成的网络，并被写入排序。它的能力得到澄清，它开始栖居在一个熟悉的世界里，那里居住着一些存在者，人们预期它们能或多或少地治疗已识别的病症。由于这些能力，无论顺境逆境，都可以把概率与这些分子联系起来；这种联系既不是纯主观的（因为它是漫长排序劳动的成果），也不是纯客观的（这种排序是假设性的），但它确实导向排序、序数尺度，并且稍加坚持，还会导向基数尺度！人们由此可以比较估计与机会，绕过奈特正确指出的问题。由此浮现出商业模式的第一版——当然还有待重新质算——其唯一目的不是计算收益或投资回报，而是表明价值可以被创造；商业模式能够质算分子，以说明在得到适当的被动化—激活之后，它们在多大程度上能够附着于一个患病、受苦的身体。为了表明这一工具何其普遍，以及大型制药公司与生物技术公司所做的质算并非例外，多甘诺娃指出，那些据以建构关系与评估的实践，可以用人类学家简·盖耶（Jane Guyer）描述非洲市场时提出的同一组概念来分析：命名、开列清单、分类、比较、建立等级，最后是赋予分数。
Nihil novum sub sole
——太阳底下无新事。这并不是说从未有新事物发生——这个分子是独一的——而更简单地说，没有什么新到不能被装备得当的能动者所质算。赫拉克利特（Heraclitus）注视的流水从不相同，但它始终是水。
IN FINANCIAL MARKETS

The qualculation tools used to evaluate goods that still have a long way to go before reaching the client for whom they are destined reach their greatest level of sophistication in the tools associated with the boom of financial markets. One could devote an entire book to financial agencies. I will limit myself here to a few of those imagined to evaluate companies and through them the goods these companies offer their clients.
在金融市场中
用于评估那些距离最终客户还很遥远的物品的质算工具，在与金融市场繁荣相关的工具中达到了最高精巧程度。人们可以用整本书来讨论金融能动者。这里我只限于其中少数几种，它们被设想用来评估公司，并通过公司评估这些公司提供给客户的物品。

How should a company be evaluated? The question is not new, and the answers are not obvious. One could move straight to considering the goods it sells and evaluating them by trying, for instance, to show what these goods do to reduce health inequality, facilitate access to essential services, and so on. The tools necessary for that type of qualculation are not inexistent, but no long investigation is required to see that they do not play an essential role in evaluating companies. The equipment that is used most corresponds to the growing influence of a form of qualculation that originates in the vision of markets imposed by a cohort of economists during the 1980s, the most prominent of whom was Milton Friedman. According to Friedman, a company’s aim is to maximize its financial value — that is to say, its value for shareholders, or, to put it another way, the price that investors are ready to pay at any given instant in order to acquire shares. The qualculation tool is financial markets themselves, where stocks are continuously appraised as they are traded. Trading floors are the main qualculative agencies, and they dominate those who would wish to institute other modes of qualculation. Friedman’s solution finally became the universal standard, just as, after many vicissitudes, the standard meter bar did in its time.

应当如何评估一家公司？这个问题并不新鲜，答案也并不显然。人们可以直接考虑公司所出售的物品，例如，通过表明这些物品如何减少健康不平等、促进基本服务的获取等来评估它们。那类质算所需的工具并非不存在，但无需长期调查便可看出，它们在评估公司时并不发挥主要作用。使用最多的装备，对应着一种质算形式日益增长的影响力；这种质算形式源自20世纪80年代一批经济学家所强加的市场观，其中最著名的是米尔顿·弗里德曼（Milton Friedman）。按照弗里德曼的观点，公司的目标是最大化其财务价值——也就是对股东的价值，或者换个说法，是投资者在任何给定时刻为取得股份而愿意支付的价格。质算工具就是金融市场本身，股票在交易过程中被持续估价。交易大厅是主要的质算能动者，它们支配着那些想要创设其他质算模式的人。弗里德曼的方案最终成为普世标准，正如标准米原器在经历诸多波折之后，也在其时代成为标准一样。
The hold this model has developed is the result of obstinate efforts, of which Marion Fourcade and Rakesh Khurana have described the main steps.

They have shown how a profession (economists) maneuvered to take over business schools, train generations of managers, control the specialized publications, and get the ear of the political and economic elites. In the end, a vast qualculative device was set up aligning managers’ interests with those of shareholders through incentives such as stock options, theoretical tools such as the theory of agency, and the promotion of takeover strategies, which create a genuine market for the control of firms. Generations of consultants went out and taught companies to recenter their activities on the center of their trade, to avoid situations of conglomerates like the plague, because they confuse shareholders, and to launch mergers and acquisitions or LBOs — leveraged buy-outs.

All this went with the introduction of accounting tools and evaluation methods that made it possible to qualculate the decisions to be made and hence to determine the qualities of goods that should be developed.
这一模式所形成的支配力，是顽强努力的结果；马里昂·富尔卡德（Marion Fourcade）与拉克什·库拉纳（Rakesh Khurana）描述了其中的主要步骤。

他们表明，一个职业群体（经济学家）如何设法接管商学院、培养一代代管理者、控制专业出版物，并让政治与经济精英听取其意见。最终，一个庞大的质算装置被建立起来，它通过股票期权等激励、代理理论等理论工具，以及对收购策略的推广，使管理者的利益与股东的利益一致；这些收购策略创造了一个真正的公司控制权市场。一代代顾问走出去，教导公司把活动重新聚焦于其本业的核心，像躲避瘟疫一样避免成为多元化企业集团，因为这种集团会让股东困惑，并教他们发起并购或 LBO——杠杆收购（leveraged buy-outs）。
所有这一切都伴随着会计工具和评估方法的引入，这些工具和方法使人能够质算所要作出的决定，并由此确定应当开发哪些物品、它们具有何种品质。
In an editorial in
Le Monde

dated April 23, 2013, written shortly before his death, Jérôme Haas, who fought his whole life to show that accounting norms should be subjected to debate, underlined the limits of these tools and the choices they insidiously impose: “Behind the technicality” of these tools, he writes, we should learn to see that “societal choices” exist, whether these are “preference for the present or awareness of the long term” — that there is a “diversity of socioeconomic models.”

He reminds us of Weber’s lesson: “Tell me how you qualculate, and I will tell you what world you live in.” Perhaps the lesson should be reversed: “Tell me what world you want to live in, and I will tell you how to qualculate.”
热罗姆·阿斯（Jérôme Haas）一生致力于表明会计规范应当接受辩论；在2013年4月23日《世界报》（
Le Monde
）一篇写于他去世前不久的社论中，他强调了这些工具的限度以及它们暗中强加的选择。他写道，在这些工具的“技术性”背后，我们应当学会看到“社会性选择”的存在，无论这些选择是“偏好当下还是意识到长期”，也应当看到“社会经济模式的多样性”。
他提醒我们记住韦伯的教训：“告诉我你如何质算，我就能告诉你，你生活在怎样的世界里。”也许这一教训应当反过来：“告诉我你想生活在怎样的世界里，我就能告诉你该如何质算。”

There is a long history of the emergence and development of stock markets that gradually found the appropriate qualculation tools, leading up to the moment when it became possible to institute financial markets as the main qualculative agencies of company values and indirectly of commercial goods. In his study of the history of stock market equipment, Alex Preda showed how important the introduction of the ticker was. As of the end of the nineteenth century, it created new forms of qualculation and new ways of making decisions in financial markets.

In its original form, the ticker is a very simple material device that receives information sent out by the financial markets and transcribes stock values in the form of continuous curves, which make it possible to follow their variations over time. For these recordings to be possible, a whole sociotechnical infrastructure had to be imagined, from noting prices, to transmitting them through the telegraph networks, to the reception by tickers distributed in different places accessible to interested professionals. With the ticker, the prices of stocks sold in one or more markets could be known and compared in far-flung places in real time. This encouraged new practices of arbitrage and speculation. Visualizing the continuous evolution of prices furthermore allowed the development of techniques of graphic analysis and opened the way for finance to be mathematized.

The ticker did not just provide information. It constructed data that, given its format, produced specific effects by suggesting certain interpretations and certain types of decisions. A curve’s shape was, indeed, interpreted as the result of aggregating a multitude of individual behavior patterns. Hence, since it was about behavior, it could suggest the hypothesis that there are underlying regularities. It made sense, then, to talk about the behavior of curves and, for instance, to imagine that one could expect reversals after certain episodes of continuous rise or fall or to consider that the existence of plateaus depended on a sequence of prior events readable in the curves. The curves, so it was thought, are signs of the existence of collective patterns of behavior and give access to the laws that govern them.
股票市场的出现与发展有一段漫长的历史，它逐渐找到了合适的质算工具，最终使金融市场有可能被创设为公司价值的主要质算能动者，并间接成为商业物品价值的主要质算能动者。亚历克斯·普雷达（Alex Preda）在研究股票市场装备史时表明，股票行情收报机（ticker）的引入何其重要。自19世纪末起，它创造了金融市场上新的质算形式和新的决策方式。

在其原初形态中，ticker 是一种非常简单的物质装置，接收金融市场发出的信息，并以连续曲线的形式转录股票价值，使人能够追踪其随时间的变化。要使这些记录成为可能，必须设想一整套社会技术基础设施：从记录价格，到通过电报网络传输价格，再到由分布在各地、相关专业人士可接触到的 ticker 接收。有了 ticker，在一个或多个市场上出售的股票价格，就可以在遥远的地方实时获知并比较。这鼓励了套利与投机的新实践。把价格的连续演变可视化，还促成了图形分析技术的发展，并为金融的数学化开辟了道路。

ticker 不仅提供信息。它建构数据；由于其格式，这些数据通过提示某些解释和某些类型的决策而产生特定效果。曲线的形状确实被解释为聚合大量个体行为模式的结果。因此，既然涉及行为，它就可以提示存在潜在规律性的假设。于是，谈论曲线的行为便有道理；例如，可以设想在某些持续上涨或下跌的片段之后会出现反转，或认为平台期的存在取决于曲线中可读的一系列先前事件。人们由此认为，曲线是集体行为模式存在的标志，并使人得以接近支配这些模式的法则。

This equipment has become ever more sophisticated. Tickers still exist, but they are now in digital form, and they trace the variations of numerous financial products. Calculating curves is standard practice with the development of big data and software technology. A whole series of data-crunching and data-processing tools have been added to the infrastructure. On the trading floor of a modern investment bank, there are also negotiating automata, telephones, price analysis software, and more. All this qualculation equipment carries categories, or worldviews, as one used to say, ways of apprehending reality and action, returns on experience that frame how companies and the goods they develop are evaluated. The equipment is collective and distributed. It would make no sense to try dissociate it or distinguish it from the traders, analysts, or investors who will decide whether to buy at this or that price on the basis of the qualculations performed. They are incorporated into one other like the soul and the brain. They are qualculative agencies.

这套装备已变得愈发精巧。ticker 仍然存在，但如今以数字形式出现，追踪众多金融产品的变动。随着大数据与软件技术的发展，计算曲线已成为常规做法。一系列数据处理与加工工具被加入基础设施。现代投资银行的交易大厅里还有自动交易装置、电话、价格分析软件等等。所有这些质算装备都承载着范畴，或人们过去常说的世界观，承载着把握现实与行动的方式，承载着经验回馈，它们框定了公司与公司所开发物品被评估的方式。装备是集体性的、分布式的。试图把它与交易员、分析师或投资者割裂开来或区分开来，是毫无意义的；后者将依据所进行的质算，决定是否以这个或那个价格买入。他们彼此嵌入，犹如灵魂与大脑。他们就是质算能动者。

These qualculative agencies do not restrict themselves to numerical calculations, even in financial markets rife with numbers, even in the era of triumphant computers. Take the case studied by Daniel Beunza and Raghu Garud of the financial analysts in the beginning of the 2000s during the internet bubble.

New businesses are appearing. They are strange beings, firms that do not (yet) have any profits and constitute difficult problems for all the experts whose job is precisely to evaluate companies’ potential. What should one think of early stage Amazon? How can this start-up, which looks like no other, be described? How can one set a price for the shares it emits or the services it promises? This case is particularly interesting because it highlights the fact that where numbers, calculations of investment profitability, and dividend expectations reign, there is no other possible strategy than qualculation.
这些质算能动者并不局限于数值计算，即便在充满数字的金融市场中，即便在计算机凯歌高奏的时代也是如此。以丹尼尔·博恩扎（Daniel Beunza）与拉古·加鲁德（Raghu Garud）研究的一个案例为例：2000年代初互联网泡沫时期的金融分析师。
新企业不断出现。它们是奇怪的存在者：一些（还）没有任何利润的公司，对所有专门评估公司潜力的专家来说都是难题。应当如何看待早期阶段的亚马逊（Amazon）？这家与任何其他公司都不像的初创企业，该如何描述？如何为它发行的股票或它承诺的服务定价？这个案例特别有趣，因为它凸显了这样一个事实：在数字、投资盈利性计算和股息预期占统治地位的地方，除了质算之外，没有其他可能的策略。

Beunza and Garud show that in the case of Amazon, the big problem for financial analysts and investors was to know how to evaluate a company that was without precedent and whose qualities were still being elaborated. What they discovered will not come as a surprise to the reader. Financial analysts qualculate the market in same way as the Yorubas described by Guyer. They try to get a perspective on the singularity of the companies they analyze, not to eliminate or deny it (you don’t kill the goose of the golden eggs), but to move forward in their qualification. To that end, they set out in search of similar cases, family resemblances, as Wittgenstein would have said, in order to produce classifications (naming) and classes (ranking) as preludes to scoring and numbering.

博恩扎与加鲁德表明，在亚马逊的案例中，金融分析师与投资者面临的重大问题是：如何评估一家没有先例、其品质仍在形成中的公司。他们的发现不会让读者感到意外。金融分析师质算市场的方式，与盖耶所描述的约鲁巴人（Yorubas）相同。他们试图对他们所分析公司的独一性形成一种视角，不是要消除或否认这种独一性（不能杀掉下金蛋的鹅），而是要在品质界定中向前推进。为此，他们出发去寻找相似案例，即维特根斯坦（Wittgenstein）所说的家族相似，以便生产分类（命名）与类别（排序），作为评分与赋数的前奏。

When Amazon was created, it initially dealt only in books. The question was whether it should be seen as a company comparable to classic bookstores, but with more powerful technology, or whether it should be put in the big family of companies born with the internet and digital technologies, companies whose essential quality was to introduce and test radically new forms of production, distribution, and consumption. Depending on the analyst, depending on how they conducted their investigations, the ways they defined the relevant traits and constructed resemblances, Amazon was profiled differently, as were the services it was supposed to provide. And depending on those choices, depending on the events that took place and were interpreted and analyzed, different modalities of qualculation were privileged. It is clear that at this stage of the analysis of market agencements, it is not a matter of determining whether or not the evaluations were correct, but rather simply of observing the qualculative practices, their diversity, and the tests to which they gave rise. As Beunza and Garud show, analyzing Amazon involved the identification, manipulation, and processing of large amounts of data, as well as the construction of classificatory frameworks and their analysis. Beunza and Garud do not study the impact of these qualculations on Amazon’s decisions, but I would guess there was plenty. (For example, in another case study, Alexandra Ouroussoff has shown how the evaluations produced by rating agencies can lead companies toward decisions that are considered to be low risk, privileging strategies of horizontal concentration or vertical integration that allow companies to show that they are in a good position to manage the competition.)

亚马逊创建之初只经营图书。问题在于，它应被视为一家与经典书店相当、但技术更强大的公司，还是应被归入随互联网与数字技术诞生的一大类公司——这类公司的本质品质是引入并试验根本上全新的生产、分配与消费形式。取决于分析师，取决于他们如何进行调查、如何界定相关特征并建构相似性，亚马逊被刻画得不同，它本应提供的服务也被刻画得不同。而且，取决于这些选择，取决于所发生并被解释和分析的事件，不同的质算方式得到优先采用。显然，在市场装配分析的这一阶段，问题不在于确定这些评估是否正确，而只在于观察质算实践、它们的多样性，以及它们所引发的检验。正如博恩扎与加鲁德所表明的，分析亚马逊涉及对大量数据的识别、操纵和处理，也涉及分类框架的建构及其分析。博恩扎与加鲁德没有研究这些质算对亚马逊决策的影响，但我猜想影响很大。（例如，在另一项案例研究中，亚历山德拉·乌鲁索夫（Alexandra Ouroussoff）表明，评级机构产生的评估如何引导公司作出被视为低风险的决策，偏爱横向集中或纵向一体化的策略，使公司得以表明自己处于能够驾驭竞争的良好位置。）

Friedman’s narrow focus on the market and the share values it is supposed to calculate ignores the thousands of diverging qualculations supported by agencies that often disagree with one another. It would have been futile for Friedman to invoke the transitory nature of this situation, for him to assert that the strength of the market lies in the fact that it always finds the true value in the end. The true value is like Minerva’s owl. It arrives once the losses and profits have been taken and once all of the qualculations have been made. The markets, because they are market agencements, live only in the transitory and know only the torment of processes.
弗里德曼狭隘地聚焦于市场以及市场本应计算的股票价值，忽视了由能动者所支撑的成千上万种彼此分歧的质算，而这些能动者常常意见不一。弗里德曼若援引这种局面的过渡性、若断言市场的力量在于它最终总能找到真实价值，那将是徒劳的。真实价值就像密涅瓦（Minerva）的猫头鹰。它要在盈亏已经落定、所有质算都已完成之后才到来。市场，由于其本身就是市场装配，只存在于过渡之中，只知道过程的煎熬。
I will return to the functioning of financial markets in Chapter 8.
我将在第八章回到金融市场的运作。
IN REINSURANCE

I encourage the reader to fill in the picture I am painting by wandering through market agencements and exploring the different profiling and scoring practices, those of banks who define and qualify loans as a function of the evaluation of potential borrowers (identification, classification, ranking, hierarchies, and so on), normalizing agencies, rating agencies, international institutions, and more. Qualculative agencies are everywhere, and everywhere they take each other on, attempting to have their qualculation methods and tools prevail.

Out of these confrontations, goods emerge, fragile and unstable, their qualities having been fixed at least temporarily. These are singular goods, rendered comparable even as they evolve to adjust to their respective intended recipients.
在再保险中
我鼓励读者在市场装配中漫游，探索不同的刻画与评分实践，以补全我所描绘的图景：银行依据对潜在借款人的评估（识别、分类、排序、等级等）来界定贷款、规定其品质；还有标准化机构、评级机构、国际机构等等。质算能动者无处不在，而且处处相互较量，力图使自己的质算方法与工具占据上风。
从这些对抗中，物品浮现出来，脆弱而不稳定，其品质至少暂时被固定下来。这些是独一的物品，它们在演化以调整自身、适应各自预定接受者的同时，也被弄得可以相互比较。

Before moving on to the analysis of the power relations between agencies, I would like simply to mention one type of qualculating agency that plays a central part in contemporary capitalist markets and that gives a striking illustration of the way market agencements function.
在转入能动者之间权力关系的分析之前，我只想提及一类质算能动者，它在当代资本主义市场中扮演核心角色，并生动地例示了市场装配的运作方式。

Until recently, the reinsurance industry had barely been studied empirically. We now have the study produced by Paula Jarzabkowski and her colleagues concerning insurance against what is nicely called “acts of God,” those “natural” catastrophes that, like earthquakes, tornadoes, cyclones, floods or fires, strike unexpectedly: “Nescitis diem neque horam” — “You do not know the day or hour.”

The problem with these exceptional catastrophes, which provoke damages worth billions of dollars, is that each of them is unique — each provokes new effects. Insurance concerning these events is a challenge to understanding and reason. The scope of the damages is such that not only can a single insurer not guarantee them, but even when a pool of insurers is constituted, reinsurers have to be found to insure the insurers.
直到不久以前，再保险业几乎未得到经验研究。现在我们有了保拉·雅扎布科夫斯基（Paula Jarzabkowski）及其同事的研究，考察针对人们美其名曰“天灾”（acts of God）的保险——那些“自然”灾难，如地震、龙卷风、气旋、洪水或火灾，出人意料地袭来：“Nescitis diem neque horam”——“你们不知道那日子，也不知道那时辰。”
这些造成数十亿美元损失的异常灾难，其问题在于每一场都是独一的——每一场都引发新的效应。为这些事件提供保险，是对理解与理性的挑战。损失范围之大，不仅单一保险公司无法承保，而且即便组成保险公司池，也必须找到再保险公司来为保险公司提供保险。

Jarzabkowski and her colleagues examine reinsurance practices in detail, with particular attention to how premiums were established. The result is fascinating. The qualculation instruments combine very sophisticated quantitative and numerical techniques, notably, statistical models that take into account considerable data of all sorts (lists of places that may be involved identified by zip code, each with its own social and geophysical characteristics, stories of remarkable events, the nature and quality of buildings, descriptions of the populations, exposure to damages and their possible costs as a function of types of catastrophes, and more). These models are partly common to the different insurers, but each adds to them and enriches them with in-house models and with particular and specific knowledge. When only very partial series are available, or even no series at all, qualiquantitative models are put together. In all cases, tables are used and filled with a series of rubrics identical to those of the statistical models, and the usual listing, regrouping, and scoring operations, based on collective work, lead to numerical evaluations. As in the case of the rating of R&D projects or therapeutic molecules, the more singular the events are, the more the work of comparing is long, complicated, and . . . necessary. The final construction is like buildings erected on quicksand, shored up with various reinforcements, grids, and crossed elements, each of which is fragile, but that, linked to one another, produce rigidity and robustness that, in the end, manage to rise and stand, at least for a while. The more unprecedented the act of God, the more bound up it is in a story that is uncertain, in Knight’s terms, and the greater the obstinacy agencies show in qualculating.

雅扎布科夫斯基及其同事详细考察再保险实践，尤其关注保费如何确定。结果引人入胜。质算工具结合了非常精巧的定量与数值技术，特别是统计模型，这些模型考虑大量各类数据（按邮政编码识别、可能涉及的地点清单，每个地点各有其社会与地球物理特征；重大事件的记载；建筑的性质与质量；人口描述；损失暴露程度及其按灾难类型估算的可能成本；等等）。这些模型部分为不同保险公司所共用，但每家都会加入自己的内部模型和特定、具体的知识，使之更加丰富。当只有非常不完整的序列、甚至完全没有序列可用时，人们便拼装出定性与定量相结合的模型。在所有情况下，人们都使用表格，填入与统计模型相同的一系列栏目，而基于集体工作的惯常开列清单、重新归组和评分操作，则导向数值评估。正如在研发项目或治疗分子的评级中那样，事件越独一，比较工作就越漫长、越复杂，也……越必要。最终的建构就像建在流沙上的建筑，用各种加固件、网格和交叉构件支撑；每一构件都脆弱，但彼此连接后便产生刚性与稳固，最终得以矗立，至少维持一段时间。天灾越是没有先例，就越被缠结在一个奈特意义上不确定的故事之中，而能动者在质算时表现出的执拗也就越大。

The authors show how in all cases, whether or not centers of big data are available, qualculating communities of experts form, trying to reach agreement as to the results of the qualculation and hence the premiums; agreement is sought not only between insurers and insured, but also between insurers and reinsurers. Unlike markets for wines and works of art, here, there is no need to dream up inexpressible subjective realities such as quality or reputation to explain how evaluations and qualifications are made. Yet in all cases, whether it be wines, contemporary art pieces, acts of God, or research and innovation projects, following the evaluating agencies, describing their qualculative practices, the instruments they use, and the communities they form is enough to understand how, in the end, an event that is by its very nature unique and singular becomes qualculable, that is to say comparable, commensurable, and subject to being given a score. The good is then profiled to turn into a commodity that can become the object of a bilateral transaction and for which, as we will see in Chapter 6 on affixing a price, a price can be given.

作者表明，在所有情况下，无论是否有大数据中心可用，都会形成由专家组成的质算共同体，力图就质算结果、并因而就保费达成一致；寻求一致不仅发生在保险人与被保险人之间，也发生在保险人与再保险人之间。与葡萄酒和艺术品市场不同，在这里无需虚构质量或声誉之类不可言说的主观现实，来解释评估与品质界定如何完成。然而在所有情况下，无论是葡萄酒、当代艺术品、天灾，还是研究与创新项目，只要跟随评估能动者，描述其质算实践、所使用的工具以及它们所形成的共同体，就足以理解：一个本质上独一而奇异的事件，最终如何变得可以质算，也就是说，可以比较、可以通约、可以被赋予分数。物品随后被刻画，以便转化为商品，成为双边交易的对象，并且正如我们将在第六章关于定价的讨论中看到的，可以为之给出一个价格。

In this section, I have mostly considered the qualculative equipment of agencies on the supply side. The agencies involved in consumption also have specialized qualculating capacities. In the next section, we will observe the power dynamics between different agencies, and I will demonstrate that consumption is not fully controlled by the supply side.
在本节中，我主要考察了供给侧能动者的质算装备。参与消费的能动者也具有专门的质算能力。在下一节中，我们将观察不同能动者之间的权力动态，我将表明消费并未被供给侧完全控制。
POWER DYNAMICS BETWEEN AGENCIES
能动者之间的权力动态

The rapid overview of qualculative agencies at work in market agencements leads to two observations. The first highlights how many agencies intervene, the second how many modes of qualculation they develop. Agencies face off in attempts to impose their qualculations and thereby the qualification of commercial goods and their modes of passiva(c)tion.
对市场装配中运作的质算能动者所作的快速巡视，引出两点观察。第一点凸显了介入其中的能动者数量之多，第二点则凸显了它们所发展的质算模式之多样。能动者彼此对峙，力图把自己的质算，并由此把商业物品的品质界定及其被动化（passiva(c)tion）模式，强加于人。

No model of qualculation is inherently superior to any other. Superiority is achieved over the course of the many confrontations between agencies that put them to the test. Superiority is always temporary, because the list of involved agencies changes, and with it, the composition of their equipment and the modalities of their qualculations also change. The qualculative power of an agency is only relational. Its definition depends on the definition of the qualculation. Its power is all the greater if the agency is in a position to
a) take a high (but finite) number of entities into account;
b) explore a rich and varied set of relations between these entities so as to establish bases for comparison and end up with groups of entities that are considered similar; and
c) elaborate competitive procedures and algorithms in order to rank these entities (ordinal numbering).
没有任何一种质算模型天生优于其他模型。优越性是在能动者之间众多使其经受检验的交锋过程中赢得的。优越性始终是暂时的，因为卷入其中的能动者名单会变化，而随着名单的变化，其装备的构成与质算的样式也会变化。一个能动者的质算之力仅仅是关系性的。它的界定取决于质算的界定。倘若一个能动者处于如下位置，它的力量就更大：
a）能够把数量众多（但有限）的实体纳入考虑；
b）探索这些实体之间丰富多样的关系，以便建立比较的基础，并最终得到被认为相似的实体群组；
c）制定有竞争力的程序与算法，以便对这些实体进行排序（序数编号）。

Market agencements constitute a space in which this qualculative confrontation can take place. The trade-off is that in these commercial arenas, certain agencies come to occupy dominant positions and to weigh heavily on the ways in which goods get qualified. Market agencements are not spaces in which agents are on an equal footing. Many agencies are without any means of qualculation and thus in very weak positions, dominated by agencies that qualculate their decisions for them and impose their mark on the design of the goods that are exchanged. The inequality and the relations of domination that structure market agencements are direct consequences of the unequal distribution of qualculation powers and thus of the asymmetries in levels of equipment.

市场装配构成了一个空间，使这种质算交锋得以在其中展开。代价是，在这些商业竞技场中，某些能动者得以占据支配位置，并对物品获得品质界定的方式施加沉重影响。市场装配并不是行动者彼此平等的空间。许多能动者没有任何质算手段，因而处于极为微弱的位置，受制于那些替它们质算其决策、并把自己的印记强加于所交换物品之设计的能动者。结构市场装配的不平等与支配关系，是质算之力分配不均的直接后果，因而也是装备水平不对称的直接后果。

Let us return to the supermarket and the emblematic encounter it organizes between the goods for sale and the shoppers. A whole slew of agencies preparing the transaction is part of the scene. Each has qualculative capacities it draws on to frame and realize the transaction. Consumers are never alone, never isolated. They are distributed. As we have seen, their evaluations involve brands and all sorts of precalculated information provided by the supermarket and its setup. These include packaging with data about the product’s composition, its origin, its labels, but also the shelving and the shelf labels, the labyrinth of aisles that propose and impose certain groupings, proximity relationships, price and quality hierarchies. Evaluations include situations, like a demonstration where the client becomes like the pedestrians being captured by the street vendors of London — or information systems — like the guidepost in the wine section that points out the vintages. Prostheses, which are designed, set up, and tested by supply-side agencies, are instruments that equip consumers and take part in the constitution of their qualculative agency. They do not, however, come to the store unprepared and destitute. Before even going into the supermarket, shoppers make shopping lists and read magazines and online consumer guides to orient their evaluations. Sometimes they even have tested the goods they are buying or share evaluations with family and friends. Furthermore, they are part of prescriptive relationships that intensify their thought processes and actions. In other words, supermarket customers are at the heart of a qualculative device that quite obviously does not exactly belong to them. As this emblematic confrontation shows, qualculative agents cannot be described as distinctly equipped entities; that is to say, one cannot claim that the equipment and tools could be divided into as many distinct families as there are different groups of agents involved. Certainly, agents come to the store with their own equipment, depending on whether they are, say, consumers or market professionals. They nevertheless also share a metrological infrastructure on which they draw as needed, depending on the circumstances.

让我们回到超市，回到它在待售物品与购物者之间组织的那场标志性相遇。整整一大群为交易作准备的能动者，都是这一幕的组成部分。每一个都拥有质算能力，并凭借这些能力来框定并实现交易。消费者从来不孤单，从来不是孤立的。他们是分布式的。如我们所见，他们的评估涉及品牌，也涉及超市及其布置所提供的形形色色预先计算好的信息。这些信息包括包装上关于产品成分、产地与标签的数据，还包括货架陈列与货架标签、过道构成的迷宫——它提示并强加某些分组方式、邻近关系以及价格与质量的等级。评估还包括情境——例如一场演示，顾客在其中就像被伦敦街头小贩招揽的行人——或者信息系统——例如葡萄酒区那块标出各年份酒的指示牌。由供给侧能动者设计、布置并测试的义肢，是装备消费者、并参与构成消费者这一质算能动者的工具。然而，消费者并不是毫无准备、一无所有地走进商店的。甚至在走进超市之前，购物者就会列购物清单，阅读杂志与在线消费者指南，以引导自己的评估。有时他们甚至已经试用过自己正要购买的商品，或与家人朋友交流过评价。此外，他们还处于各种规定性关系之中，这些关系强化了他们的思维过程与行动。换言之，超市顾客处于一个质算装置的核心，而这个装置显然并不完全属于他们。正如这场标志性对峙所示，质算行动者不能被描述为装备彼此分明的实体；也就是说，人们不能声称，装备与工具可以按照所涉行动者群体的数目，划分为同样多的不同族类。当然，行动者带着自己的装备来到商店，这取决于他们是消费者还是市场专业人士，如此等等。然而，他们同时也共享一套计量基础设施，并视情境按需从中取用。
AUTONOMY AND HETERONOMY

Granted, when customers amble around a supermarket, they are surrounded by multiple devices that assist them in qualifying, classifying, and making hierarchies of the goods on offer, but these devices have mainly been designed, tested, and implemented without their having been directly involved in their design: buyers evaluate goods, but they use calculation tools that have been more or less explicitly offered or even imposed. As they inspect the shelves, read labels, guides, or instruction manuals, the customer continues a calculation that was started and framed by qualification professionals. Shoppers qualculate heteronomously.
自主与他律
诚然，当顾客在超市里闲逛时，他们周围环绕着众多装置，协助他们对所售物品进行品质界定、分类并排出等级；但这些装置主要是在他们未直接参与设计的情况下被设计、测试和实施的：购买者评估物品，却使用那些或多或少被明确提供、甚至被强加的计算工具。当他们查看货架、阅读标签、指南或使用说明时，顾客所延续的是一项由品质界定专业人士启动并框定的计算。购物者是在他律状态下进行质算的。

This notion of heteronomous qualculation is important. In commercial arenas, it would be exceptional to have a face-off between some agencies that qualculate and others that do not. Indeed, to make their qualculations, some agencies depend heavily on the equipment designed and implemented by the very agencies they are facing in the marketplace. It is as though in a chess game, one of the players gradually colonized his opponent’s brain so that the latter, while continuing what he experienced as his game, ended up being played more than playing. A particularly striking example of this transition from an autonomous to a heteronomous position is the one Pierre Bourdieu studies in his remarkable analysis of the real-estate market.

He describes how the meeting between the seller and the potential buyer becomes a showdown in which the former tries to impose his own calculation tools on the latter, often successfully. The buyers arrive with a series of criteria for choosing an apartment: location, proximity to public transportation and schools, number of rooms, price, but in the end, they adopt the criteria proposed by the seller. After the meeting, the buyers adopt the tools the seller presented in order to optimize the managing of their budget and to evaluate the qualities of the properties being offered.

他律质算（heteronomous qualculation）这一概念很重要。在商业竞技场中，若一方能动者进行质算、另一方不进行质算，这样的对峙会是例外。事实上，为了完成质算，某些能动者严重依赖的，正是它们在市场上所面对的那些能动者所设计并实施的装备。这就好比在一盘国际象棋中，其中一位棋手逐步殖民了对手的大脑，以致后者虽然继续体验着属于自己的棋局，最终却更多是被下，而不是在下棋。皮埃尔·布迪厄（Pierre Bourdieu）在其对房地产市场的出色分析中，研究了一个从自主位置转向他律位置的尤为醒目的例子。
他描述了卖方与潜在买方之间的会面如何变成一场摊牌，前者力图把自己的计算工具强加给后者，而且往往成功。买方带着一系列挑选公寓的标准而来：地段、靠近公共交通与学校、房间数量、价格，但最终，他们采纳的是卖方提出的标准。会面之后，买方采用卖方展示的工具，以优化其预算管理，并评估待售房产的品质。

One of the strategies implemented to lead an agent to qualculate in a predictable way involves organizing experiments during which they are cut offfrom all other equipment. This strategy has long been in use in the food industry, as well as in sectors such as perfume, in which the goods are primarily addressed to senses with which a human body is “naturally” equipped in order to evaluate. How can a person be made into a mere nose, induced to evaluate fragrances on offer positively? How can a customer who buys a readymade meal or sits down at a restaurant table be reduced to the association of sensations that lead him to a positive appreciation of the food served to him? To answer these questions, full-scale tests are organized in order to identify the agencements that get through to the bodies and minds of the people targeted by limiting mediations and by preventing recourse to other qualculative resources.

为引导行动者以可预测的方式进行质算，所实施的策略之一，是组织实验，在实验中把他们与所有其他装备隔绝开来。这一策略在食品工业中早已使用，在香水这类部门中也是如此：在这些部门，物品主要针对的是人体为了评估而“天然”配备的感官。如何把一个人变成单纯的鼻子，诱导他对所提供的香氛作出正面评价？如何把一个购买现成餐食、或在餐馆桌旁坐下的顾客，化约为一组感觉的联合，使他对自己被端上的食物产生正面鉴赏？为回答这些问题，人们组织按实际规模进行的测试，以便通过限制中介、阻止诉诸其他质算资源，识别出那些能够通达目标人群身体与心智的装配。

With the development of the neurosciences, these strategies are poised to become frighteningly effective. Whereas work on sensations and their expression used to draw on a method close to bricolage, there is now, in a much bolder way, a real program to equip the brain. The challenge is to “cleanse” test consumers so they become essentially a brain that is hooked up, controllable, and concentrated on the qualculation of the sensations their bodies transmit in such a way that the qualculative chain (which has to recognize and score the qualities of the goods submitted to it) is not distracted by fortuitous emotions, fits of conscience, or collateral misgivings that might make the qualculation deviate in unpredictable directions.

随着神经科学的发展，这些策略有望变得令人恐惧地有效。以往关于感觉及其表达的研究所借助的方法近乎拼凑（bricolage），如今则出现了一个大胆得多的真正纲领，要对大脑进行装备。挑战在于“清洗”受试消费者，使他们本质上成为一个被接入、可控制的大脑，专注于对其身体所传递的感觉进行质算，从而使其质算链条（它必须识别并给提交给它的物品品质打分）不被偶然的情绪、良心的发作或附带的不安所干扰——这些干扰可能使质算偏离到不可预测的方向。

Many university laboratories are working hard to find a viable answer to this challenge; before imagining the devices that would reproduce what happens in the lab on commercial sites, they seek to determine the conditions under which neurosubjects emerge. Yes, it does seem possible to achieve this short circuit by choosing the right prostheses. After all, we have all seen the emblematic success of Stephen Hawking, affected by that terrible disease amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, which paralyzes the body while leaving cerebral capacities intact.

This pathology achieves what all neuromarketing experts are striving for — that is to say, the creation of a chimera, or a cyborg, if you prefer, made of a human brain hooked up to equipment that feels with and for him, that thinks with and for him, and that floods him with data that he has only to appropriate in order to finish the qualculation. Neurosciences are trying to extend what Stephen Hawking (with all his human and nonhuman assistants) showed — namely, that a human person reduced to a brain can be enhanced into an agency that qualculates the laws of physics and the universe.

Since their aim is much more modest, there is no reason to think they will not succeed. It is not a matter of equipping a qualculative agency to reconcile quantum physics with general relativity, but more simply and prosaically of designing an agency that, given a choice between two ready-made meals, predictably opts for the one that, after a long series of tests, has been designed so as to affect his brain as powerfully as possible.
许多大学实验室正在努力寻找应对这一挑战的可行答案；在设想出能在商业场所复制实验室中所发生之事的装置之前，他们先要确定神经主体得以涌现的条件。是的，通过选择合适的义肢，实现这种短路似乎确实是可能的。毕竟，我们都见过斯蒂芬·霍金（Stephen Hawking）的标志性成功：他罹患那种可怕的疾病——肌萎缩侧索硬化，它使身体瘫痪，却让大脑能力保持完好。

这种病症实现了所有神经营销专家都在追求的东西——也就是说，创造出一个嵌合体，或者如果你愿意，也可以说一个赛博格：它由一颗人脑与一套装备相连而成，这套装备与他一起、并替他感受，与他一起、并替他思考，还向他灌注大量数据，他只需将这些数据据为己有，便可完成质算。神经科学正试图扩展斯蒂芬·霍金（连同他所有的人类与非人类助手）所展示的东西——即，一个被化约为大脑的人，可以被增强为一个能够质算物理学定律与宇宙的能动者。
既然他们的目标要谦逊得多，就没有理由认为他们不会成功。问题并不在于装备一个质算能动者，好让量子物理与广义相对论调和起来，而更为简单、更为平淡：设计一个能动者，使他在两份现成餐食之间作选择时，可以预测地选择那份经过一长串测试、被设计得能尽可能强烈地作用于其大脑的餐食。

In a study worth reading, STS scholar Steve Woolgar and his colleagues show how these neuromarketers reach their goal of stripping the human agent of everything that might lead him away from being the feeling brain they want him to be.

Granted, the laboratory device that makes this possible is still a little cumbersome and complicated. But one should never despair of technology! Ways will no doubt be found to transpose and transport this sociotechnical environment and to multiply and disseminate these new qualculative agencies. Perhaps hooked-up, assisted brains will eventually shop at the neighborhood supermarket or wait for a delivery to arrive at the front door.
在一项值得一读的研究中，科学技术研究（STS）学者史蒂夫·伍尔加（Steve Woolgar）及其同事表明，这些神经营销者如何达成其目标：剥除人类行动者身上一切可能使他偏离他们所要的那个“感受大脑”的东西。
诚然，使这一切成为可能的实验室装置仍然有些笨重和复杂。但永远不应对技术绝望！无疑会找到办法，把这一社会技术环境移植并搬运出去，使这些新的质算能动者倍增并扩散开来。也许有一天，被接入、受辅助的大脑会在社区超市购物，或在前门等待送货上门。

Dissymmetries do not always develop in the same direction, and their hold is never complete or irreversible. Jean Lave and her colleagues have shown that there are very simple behaviors of resistance that allow the consumer to at least partially escape the qualculative powers of the suppliers. Even if a human agent does not explicitly have recourse to arithmetic while shopping, that does not mean they do not qualculate.

A very widespread device, for instance, involves allocating various amounts to different categories of purchases: all agencies qualculate, more and more intensely. Furthermore, if we stick to considering only the relations between the agencies involved in a bilateral transaction, then either the buyer or the seller is in the position to dominate qualculation. Only a case-by-case analysis of the relations can determine whether there is autonomy or heteronomy. In certain cases, an institutional customer purchasing a complex product from an investment bank (let’s say, a strategy for fiscal optimization or a contract covering exchange-rate risks) will have no visibility as to the real structure of the product or the way the bank charges and covers it; they will qualculate the product with the seller’s instruments. In other cases, a multinational corporation’s financial department will appeal to several banks, creating competition between funders, and will impose its own qualculation instruments without understanding the global strategy of the banking sector.
不对称并不总是朝同一方向发展，其掌控也从来不是完整或不可逆的。让·拉夫（Jean Lave）及其同事已经表明，存在着非常简单的抵抗行为，使消费者至少能部分逃脱供给方的质算之力。即便人类行动者在购物时并不明确诉诸算术，也并不意味着他们不进行质算。

例如，一种非常普遍的手法，是把不同数额分配给不同类别的采购：所有能动者都在质算，而且越来越密集地质算。此外，如果我们只考虑参与双边交易的能动者之间的关系，那么支配质算的既可能是买方，也可能是卖方。只有对关系作逐案分析，才能确定究竟存在自主还是他律。在某些情况下，一个机构客户从投资银行购买复杂产品（比如说，一项税务优化策略，或一份覆盖汇率风险的合约），对产品的真实结构、或银行如何收费与对冲，都没有能见度；他们将用卖方的工具来质算该产品。在另一些情况下，一家跨国公司的财务部门会求助于多家银行，在资金提供者之间制造竞争，并在不理解银行业整体战略的情况下，强加自己的质算工具。

The relation of autonomy or heteronomy between qualculative agencies is obviously subject to variations, since it is actualized over the course of qualification trials. An agency can alternate between different equipment, change qualculation instruments during a transaction, modify its equipment to become more powerful, or, on the contrary, it can decide to adopt another agency’s tools. Let us not forget that an agency’s equipment can include tools and procedures for revising the very evaluations it has itself produced. This is frequent in the case of heavily equipped agencies such as financial institutions that have the means to put different qualculation tools in competition with one another. It is no less frequent, however, when the qualculation equipment is light: shifts are easier and situation reversals are more frequent and . . . spectacular.

质算能动者之间的自主或他律关系显然会发生变化，因为它是在品质界定检验的过程中被现实化的。一个能动者可以在不同装备之间交替，在交易过程中更换质算工具，改造自己的装备以变得更强，或者相反，决定采纳另一个能动者的工具。不要忘记，一个能动者的装备可以包括用于修正它自己所作评估的工具与程序。在装备雄厚的能动者那里，这很常见，例如金融机构有办法让不同的质算工具相互竞争。然而，在质算装备轻便时，这种情况同样常见：转换更容易，局势逆转更频繁，而且……更富戏剧性。

In this connection, it is appropriate to remember the useful distinction between a planned buy and an impulse buy in a supermarket. In the former, the customer has a greater autonomy, relying on equipment (such as lists, information gleaned on the web, friends’ advice) that is prepared ahead of time and depends less on the store’s equipment. The latter corresponds instead to a heteronomous position: the consumer, strolling without any particular intention, is taken in by the calculating device created by marketing experts; the consumer becomes, as it were, an annex of this arrangement. Recent research on electronic commerce indicates that web users tend to adopt the first type of behavior, but that supply agencies like Amazon react in such a way as to flip them into heteronomy. As sociologist Christian Licoppe concludes: “The practices of the ‘connected’ consumer are neither determined in advance (as in the logic of planned purchasing) nor manipulated by the market environment, even with the consumer’s consent (as in the logic of impulse buying). The conduct of one’s acts of consumption oscillates between flexible guidance and opportunistic flexibility.”

Whatever the case, a consumer can always (in principle) change provider, walk out of the supermarket, and check out the competition. This possibility obviously depends on the circumstances and in particular on the strategies deployed by the various competing sellers. As will be seen in Chapter 6, in sectors where an overwhelming majority of sellers are heavily equipped, consumers and users have no choice but to accept the state of being dominated.

在这方面，应当记住超市中计划性购买与冲动性购买之间那个有用的区分。在前一种情况下，顾客拥有更大的自主性，依靠的是事先准备好的装备（如清单、从网上搜集的信息、朋友的建议），较少依赖商店的装备。后一种情况则对应一种他律位置：消费者漫无目的地闲逛，被营销专家创造的计算装置所俘获；可以说，消费者成了这一安排的附属物。晚近关于电子商务的研究表明，网络用户倾向于采取第一种行为，但像亚马逊这样的供给侧能动者会作出反应，把他们翻转为他律状态。正如社会学家克里斯蒂安·利科佩（Christian Licoppe）所总结的：“‘联网’消费者的实践，既不是预先被决定的（如计划性购买的逻辑），也不是被市场环境操纵的——即便得到消费者同意（如冲动性购买的逻辑）。其消费行为的展开，在灵活引导与机会主义的灵活性之间摆动。”
无论如何，消费者总是（原则上）可以更换供应商、走出超市、去比较竞争对手。这种可能性显然取决于具体情境，尤其取决于各个相互竞争的卖方所部署的策略。正如第六章将会看到的那样，在绝大多数卖方都装备雄厚的部门，消费者与用户别无选择，只能接受被支配的状态。
OUTSOURCING QUALCULATIVE CAPACITIES
In order to increase its qualculating power, an agency can choose to incorporate or use the qualculations made by other agencies.
外包质算能力
为了提高自己的质算之力，一个能动者可以选择吸纳或使用其他能动者所作的质算。

Let us return to the simple case of the encounter between consumer and seller within the framework of a commercial device at the moment when the bilateral transaction is concluded. A customer who walks into a supermarket is not facing an isolated qualculative agency, but rather a formidable association of agencies that have had the time and the means to coordinate their efforts and their qualculations in such a way as to make them almost unassailable. How could I, in front of shelves full of goods, redo a qualculation whose first operations were launched on faraway sites to which I have no access and were then taken up again a thousand times in other places, transformed, amended, tested, to elaborate a history of which there is sometimes a trace on the packaging, covered in data and analysis results and proudly flaunting a quality label? How could I be in any position to produce my own evaluation of this enigmatic, mysterious product? The only solution is to be prepared for the confrontation. I may first mobilize all the information and data qualculated by other agencies that are better equipped than I, such as consumer groups, internet sites with user reviews, evaluations provided by a network of friends, guides, and so on. I can also refer to my own experiences and prior purchases. The use of cell phones in supermarkets is more and more common as people turn to them to get an opinion from a friend in real time or check a site on the web for comparative reviews. The commercial force deployed by the supermarket is likely to anticipate my questions and to mobilize other results, evaluations, and qualculations immediately, depending on the questions or objections I may raise. What is at stake in this confrontation of forces is the number of connections an agency has established or can establish. This observation echoes one of the main results of social-network analysis: the more central an agent, the greater his influence. The isolated agent who can count only on himself, that is to say, on almost nothing, is barred from qualculation. To understand how such a situation came about, we should return to the definition of qualculation and its conditions of possibility. To make a good nonqualculable, it is enough, for instance, to prevent closure of the list of entities to be considered, or to facilitate the proliferation of relations between these entities, or to paralyze any attempt at classification. This would be a simple, but costly strategy that would aim at leading the dominated agency astray, into a labyrinth of relations from which there is no exit, thus reducing its agency to impotence, limiting it to its own somatic resources.

让我们回到一个简单的情形：在商业装置的框架内，消费者与卖方相遇，双边交易达成的那一刻。走进超市的顾客所面对的，并不是一个孤立的质算能动者，而是一个令人生畏的能动者联合体；这些能动者有时间和手段协调其努力与质算，使这些质算几乎无懈可击。面对摆满物品的货架，我怎么可能重做一次质算？这次质算的最初操作，是在我无法进入的遥远场所启动的，随后又在其他地方被接续了上千次，经过转化、修正、测试，编织出一段历史——这段历史有时在包装上留下痕迹：包装布满数据与分析结果，并骄傲地展示着一个品质标签。我怎么可能有能力对这个谜一般、神秘莫测的产品作出自己的评估？唯一的办法，是为这场对峙做好准备。我可以首先调动那些装备比我更好的其他能动者所质算的全部信息与数据，例如消费者团体、带用户评论的网站、朋友网络提供的评价、指南，等等。我也可以参照自己的经验与先前的购买经历。在超市里使用手机越来越普遍，人们会实时向朋友征求意见，或上网查看比较性评论。超市所部署的商业力量，很可能预见到我的问题，并根据我可能提出的疑问或异议，立即调动其他结果、评价与质算。这场力量交锋的赌注，是一个能动者已经建立或能够建立的连接数量。这一观察呼应社会网络分析的主要结果之一：一个行动者越处于中心，其影响力越大。孤立的行动者只能依靠自己，也就是说，几乎无所依靠，因而被挡在质算之外。要理解这样的局面如何形成，我们应当回到质算的定义及其可能性条件。要让一件物品变得不可质算，办法很简单，例如阻止待考虑实体名单的封闭，或促成这些实体之间关系的增殖，或使任何分类的尝试陷于瘫痪。这将是一种简单却代价高昂的策略，旨在把被支配的能动者引入歧途，引入一座没有出口的关系迷宫，从而使其能动性归于无能，把它限制在自身的躯体资源之内。

Since I refer to the autonomy and heteronomy of qualculation capabilities or to their cross-mobilization, I would like to underline that each agency integrates (at least to a certain extent) the evaluations (or elements of evaluation) made by other agencies into its own evaluations. The integration is maximal when one of them is condemned to heteronomy. It is partial, in varying degrees, in the opposite case. Furthermore, since agencies enter into alliances and subcontracting relations, these relations establish a qualculation space in which each agency shares its equipment with others, little by little, and necessarily takes their qualculations into account. We will come back to this question later.

既然我谈到质算能力的自主与他律，或谈到它们的交叉调动，我想强调：每个能动者都会把其他能动者所作的评估（或评估要素）整合进自己的评估之中（至少在一定程度上如此）。当其中一个能动者被迫处于他律状态时，这种整合达到最大。在相反的情况下，整合则是部分的，程度不一。此外，由于能动者会结成联盟、建立分包关系，这些关系确立了一个质算空间；在其中，每个能动者一点一点地与他人分享自己的装备，并必然把他人的质算纳入考虑。我们稍后会回到这个问题。

These strategic interdependences are easy to identify in the reality of commercial activities. Consumer groups organize tests to compare and rank this or that family of goods, tests that mirror at least some of the characteristics and evaluations declared by the producers and resellers, who also integrate elements into their evaluations in anticipation of consumer groups’ tests. These crossed anticipations, leading in some cases to consensual descriptions of the qualculated goods, can be found in all sectors of market agencements. They are common practice in financial activities (the very notion of speculation and the tools it uses imply such anticipations) and in the competition between agencies over market share. Economic theory has long since picked up on these crossed anticipations through game theory. However, the analysis can still be broadened by looking beyond the sellers and buyers to the multiple agencies involved upstream and downstream, with their diversity of equipment for shaping and framing anticipations. And let’s not forget agencies in what might be called collateral positions, such as governments and legal institutions.

这些战略性的相互依赖，在商业活动的现实中很容易识别。消费者团体组织测试，对某一类物品进行比较与排序；这些测试至少映现出生产者和经销商所宣称的某些特征与评价，而后者在作评估时也会预判消费者团体的测试，并因此纳入某些要素。这些交叉预期——在某些情况下导致对质算物品形成共识性描述——可以在市场装配的所有部门中找到。它们在金融活动中（投机的概念本身及其所使用的工具就蕴含着这类预期）以及在能动者争夺市场份额的竞争中，都是常见做法。经济理论早已通过博弈论把握了这些交叉预期。然而，分析还可以进一步拓宽：不仅看卖方与买方，还要看上下游卷入的众多能动者，以及它们塑造和框定预期的装备的多样性。也不要忘记那些可以说处于旁侧位置的能动者，例如政府与法律机构。
RELATIONSHIP DYNAMICS IN QUALCULATION

The power dynamics between agencies are not set in stone. To reverse an asymmetry between qualculative powers and flip the power relations, agencies can acquire new equipment, fight to establish devices that increase their autonomy, seek to establish connections and alliances with other agencies, or if necessary, take on the design of new qualculation equipment.
质算中的关系动态
能动者之间的权力动态并非一成不变。要逆转质算之力之间的不对称、翻转权力关系，能动者可以获取新装备，力争建立能增强其自主性的装置，寻求与其他能动者建立连接与联盟，或者必要时承担新质算装备的设计。

Management studies scholar Peter Karnøe followed the construction of a nuclear plant in southern England over the course of eight years (2007 to 2015). During this period, the government changed the framework for evaluation, and therefore the qualculation tools, three times in order to build new alliances and maintain the balance of power.

In the first evaluation, the hypothesis was that the price of natural gas and taxes on carbon emissions would grow: a simple calculation — based on the LCOE (leveled cost of electricity), the cost divided by the annual production over the life of the plant — showed that no public funding for the plant was necessary. Both Labour and the Conservatives supported the project. A few years later, however, the government defined a new framework when it faced the objections leveled by those who considered the observed decline in gas prices and the collapse of the market for carbon emission permits to be long-term phenomena. Critics held that nuclear electricity would therefore turn out to be more expensive than competing sources of energy. In that moment, the government no longer emphasized the absence of public funding as a criterion for evaluation, but insisted instead on supply security and the promotion of noncarbon technologies. The government then offered to guarantee a price that would protect the plant owner from a price drop in alternative energies. The opposition denounced the return to a policy of public subsidy and made an issue of the irrational and risky nature of predictions and commitments over more than half a century. So the government changed the evaluation framework and tools yet again. At this point, it insisted that the capacity to provide electricity no matter the circumstances or historical contingencies, the ability to “keep the lights on” while creating twenty-five thousand jobs, was the real stake of the plant. In 2020, as I write this, the story is far from over. Objections to the reactor vessels have now entered the debate. Steel, which had not had a place in the evaluation matrix, has become one of the main actors: uncontrolled migrations of carbon are seriously compromising the plant’s security. And as the final straw, even within EDF, the French state company to whom the program was entrusted, there are voices denouncing inept decision making by the general management, which had the company take on a ruinous project. EDF’s financial director has resigned.
管理学研究学者彼得·卡恩厄（Peter Karnøe）追踪了英格兰南部一座核电站的建设，历时八年（2007年至2015年）。在此期间，政府三次更改评估框架，并因而更改质算工具，以建立新的联盟并维持权力平衡。

在第一次评估中，假设是天然气价格与碳排放税将上涨：一项简单的计算——基于 LCOE（平准化电力成本，即电站寿命期内的总成本除以总发电量）——表明该电站无需公共资金。工党与保守党都支持该项目。然而几年后，面对那些认为所观察到的天然气价格下跌与碳排放许可市场崩溃属于长期现象的人所提出的反对意见，政府界定了新的框架。批评者认为，核电因此将比竞争性能源更昂贵。此时，政府不再强调“无需公共资金”作为评估标准，转而强调供应安全与推广非碳技术。政府随后提出担保一个价格，使电站所有者免受替代能源价格下跌的影响。反对派谴责这是重回公共补贴政策，并拿半个多世纪以上的预测与承诺所具有的不理性与风险性大做文章。于是政府再次更换了评估框架与工具。这一次，它坚持认为，无论情况如何、历史偶然性如何都能提供电力的能力，即在创造两万五千个就业岗位的同时“让灯继续亮着”的能力，才是该电站的真正赌注。2020年，也就是我写作此书的此刻，事情远未结束。对反应堆压力容器的反对意见如今已进入辩论。钢铁此前在评估矩阵中没有位置，如今却成了主要行动者之一：不受控制的碳迁移正在严重危及电站安全。而最要命的是，甚至在受托实施该项目的法国国有企业法国电力公司（EDF）内部，也有声音谴责最高管理层决策无能，使公司承接了一个注定亏本的项目。EDF 的财务总监已经辞职。

From a story full of twists and surprises, Karnøe extracts a few essential lessons. First, he observes that the evaluation depends entirely on the frameworks that guide it and the tools that are used. That is not, however, the main point. According to him, the successive transformations of the evaluation frameworks show that the dynamics of the power balance between agencies cannot be dissociated from the implementation of the qualculation tools that they design and choose. These evaluation frameworks should not be considered simple rhetorical artifices. One of their very real properties is indeed that they account for the balance of power and contribute to its recomposition by creating space for new coalitions.
卡恩厄从这个充满曲折与意外情节的故事中提炼出几条根本教益。首先，他观察到，评估完全取决于引导它的框架以及所使用的工具。然而，这并不是要点。在他看来，评估框架的历次变化表明，能动者之间权力平衡的动态，不能与它们所设计并选择的质算工具的实施相分离。这些评估框架不应被视为简单的修辞伎俩。它们的一项非常真实的属性恰恰是：它们反映权力平衡，并通过为新联盟创造空间，参与权力平衡的重组。

The geopolitical significance of qualculative powers is perhaps most visible in the financial world. One of the specific characteristics of this activity is indeed to make possible important changes in the relative size of actors; these changes can seem surprising, compared with other more industrial or more patrimonial forms of capitalism. This observation encourages us to relativize the relevance of a tradition inscribed throughout the social sciences that tends to consider different resources or types of capital available to agents as the breeding ground for power relations and domination. This type of approach is ill adapted to the analysis of market agencements, since, as we saw, the existence of capital, or the value of capital, depends on the qualculation equipment used. What is at stake for domination is not, then, the appropriation of capital, but rather of the qualculating equipment; in particular, what is at stake is the equipment that frames and supports
capitalization

processes — that is to say, the equipment that authorizes the assertion “this is capital” and that imposes the measure of it. Without accounting tools transforming an activity, or an entity into an asset whose value is decreed to be equal to the sum of the actualized revenues it produces, neither capital nor accumulation would exist.

The asymmetries produced by the unequal distribution of this accumulation would therefore not exist, either. Capital, as a resource and as a value, is a result of the capacity to impose the calculation of its value, not vice versa. This explains that the measure of capital can be a good substitute for the measure of power only in situations of status quo, or, if you prefer, of solid agreement on the modes of calculation.

质算之力的地缘政治意义，或许在金融世界中最为可见。这一活动的一项具体特征，确实是使行动者的相对规模发生重大变化成为可能；与资本主义其他更具工业性或更以家族财产为基础的形式相比，这些变化可能显得令人惊讶。这一观察促使我们相对化一种贯穿社会科学的传统的相关性：这一传统倾向于把行动者可支配的不同资源或资本类型，视为权力关系与支配的温床。这类进路不适用于分析市场装配，因为如我们所见，资本的存在、或资本的价值，取决于所使用的质算装备。因此，支配的赌注并不是对资本的占有，而是对质算装备的占有；尤其关键的是那些框定并支撑
资本化
过程的装备——也就是说，那些授权人们断言“这是资本”、并强制规定其度量方式的装备。如果没有会计工具把一项活动、或一个实体转化为一项资产，并规定其价值等于它所产生之折现后的收益的总和，那么既不会有资本，也不会有积累。
因此，由这种积累的不平等分配所产生的不对称，也就不会存在。资本，作为资源与作为价值，是强制推行其价值计算的能力所产生的结果，而不是相反。这解释了为什么只有在现状（status quo）之下，或者如果你愿意，在对计算模式存在牢固共识的情况下，资本的度量才能很好地替代权力的度量。

Taking notice of qualculation equipment in commercial activities highlights why inequalities cannot be accounted for solely on the basis of information and information asymmetry. Information does not exist independently of its production and shaping. In certain markets, the problem is not access to information, but rather access to control over the design and implementation of all the tools and devices that allow observations to be made, observations to be transformed into data, and information fed into the qualculating practices that result in decision making. Relations of domination that permeate and structure markets are inscribed in the relations of qualculation. This point of view is not new. However, it has become inescapable. Indeed, it is more and more difficult to pretend that commercial transactions take place between equals when the means for the qualculations through which goods are evaluated have become objects of experimentation and subjects of debates that render visible the asymmetries they harbor, as is the case in financial markets or mass distribution. One can and must therefore include in the analysis the increasingly numerous programs that tend toward providing new tools for agencies whose qualculative power is weak, or that tend toward increasing the qualculative power of the strongest, or, indeed, that tend toward changing the very rules of the game by introducing skills that require new criteria or new formulas, disqualifying the old ones. Recourse to wide debates, such as the one organized in France in 2013 around energy transition, aims to mobilize the most diverse skills and expertise and thus to widen the market agencements
until they are able to integrate new

qualculative agencies and to contradict those who had had a monopoly on evaluation operations. The design of new qualculation equipment has become a full-fledged activity. It constitutes a strategic stake in engineering market agencements, and it mobilizes wide communities of experts and specialists whose activity should be studied . . . and assessed.

关注商业活动中的质算装备，凸显了为什么不平等不能仅仅依据信息与信息不对称来解释。信息并不独立于其生产与塑形而存在。在某些市场中，问题不在于获取信息，而在于获取对以下一切工具与装置之设计与实施的控制权：这些工具与装置使观察得以进行，使观察转化为数据，使信息进入质算实践，并最终导致决策。渗透并结构市场的支配关系，铭刻在质算关系之中。这一观点并不新颖。然而，它已变得无可回避。事实上，当物品评估所经由的质算手段已成为实验对象与辩论主题，并由此显露出其所蕴含的不对称时——金融市场或大众分销的情形即是如此——越来越难以假装商业交易发生在平等者之间。因此，人们可以而且必须把越来越多这样的纲领纳入分析：它们致力于为质算之力薄弱的能动者提供新工具，或致力于增强最强者的质算之力，又或者致力于通过引入需要新标准或新公式的技能、使旧标准失效，来改变游戏规则本身。诉诸广泛辩论——例如2013年法国围绕能源转型组织的辩论——旨在调动最多样的技能与专业知识，从而拓宽市场装配，
直到它们能够整合新的
质算能动者，并反驳那些曾垄断评估操作的人。新质算装备的设计已成为一项成熟的活动。它构成工程化市场装配的一项战略赌注，并调动广泛的专家与专门人士共同体，他们的活动应当被研究……并被评估。
QUALCULATION DEVICES ARE THE EQUIPMENT OF A HABITUS
质算装置是惯习的装备

The dominant never have as strong a hold as when the dominated have the impression they are the authors of their own choices. This is Bourdieu’s notion of symbolic violence, a powerful contribution to the analysis of an apparently paradoxical situation. The operator that makes sense of this paradox is the “habitus,” a set of durable and transposable dispositions that creates an “autonomy” that is only the illusory consequence of a situation of heteronomy. The habitus explains why and how agents generate choices that are merely the consequences of causal chains that escape them. Does this explanation still hold when one includes qualculation equipment in the analysis, the mostly extrasomatic equipment that Bourdieu only barely takes into account? Indeed it does! If we agree to extend the notion of habitus to qualculation instruments, I believe it is easier to explain why and how certain evaluating practices endure, even as they transform.

当被支配者自以为是自己选择之作者的时候，支配者的掌控最为牢固。这就是布迪厄（Pierre Bourdieu）的符号暴力（violence symbolique）概念，它是对一种看似悖谬的处境所作的有力分析贡献。使这一悖论得到理解的操作项，是“惯习”（habitus）：一套持久而可移置的性情倾向，它制造出一种“自主性”，而这种自主性不过是他律（hétéronomie）处境所造成的幻觉后果。惯习解释了行动者为何以及如何作出一些选择，而这些选择不过是逃逸于他们之外的因果链的后果。当我们把质算装备——那种大体上位于身体之外、布迪厄几乎不曾加以考虑的装备——纳入分析时，这一解释是否仍然成立？确实成立！如果我们同意把惯习概念扩展到质算工具，我相信就更容易解释某些评估实践为何以及如何在转化的同时得以持存。
Take the case of Amazon’s recommendation engine. I will illustrate with an anecdote from my personal experience.

倘若我不假思索地点开维勒贝克、下单，下一分钟就在我的 Kindle 上收到这本书，那我就是把亚马逊的质算据为己有了。选择是我的：没有任何东西迫使我这样做，我却点了下去；然而这一选择并不属于我，它是由亚马逊呈现给我的：“您可能还喜欢。”我的惯习让我能够对新处境迅速作出反应，它替我作了决定，但这是一种被亚马逊及其算法以不断演化的方式结构起来的惯习。如果我与亚马逊隔绝，我会作出不同的选择；如果说存在某种惯习，那它确实是一种正处于重新编程过程中的惯习。

I did not in fact double-click. The equipment Amazon makes available to me and that I use so often has become an extension of my own body and my own mind. Yet it is not the only equipment on which, and with which, I can count. Other sociocognitive prostheses are also available to me, such as the ones I have mentioned in this chapter, that can be activated at any time. First there is my own experience as a reader. Not only is a habitus less rigid than sociology has portrayed it to be; it is even more pliant once it is attached to a qualculative apparatus that is itself a programmable infrastructure.

The more the equipment that is available to me (and that avails itself of me) proliferates, becomes more complex, fragmented, and segmented, the more the extrasomatic resources become instrumental, the more that reprogramming, because it is always about reprogramming, becomes hard to follow, predict, and control. An agency’s autonomy, which of course does not mean its independence, since the equipment is there and qualculates, depends on the range and complexity of the equipment available to it.
